IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r6.claim: Some classify ضالا in 93:7 as the opposite of guidance, and Ibn Qutayba is among them.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r6.anchor: وقد جعل قوم هذه الآية من الضلال الذي هو ضد الهدى منهم ، ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r7.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī explain the phrase as finding the Prophet among a misguided people and guiding him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r7.anchor: عن الفراء والكسائي : أن معناها : ووجدك في قوم ضلال فهداك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r8.speaker: السائل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r8.claim: The questioner rejects al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī's explanation as unconvincing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r8.anchor: فقال السائل : ليس هذا بمقنع عندي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r9.speaker: ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r9.claim: Thaʿlab calls his alternative correct and links ضال to forgetfulness, reasoning from the two women in the debt verse, one of whom may need the other to remind her.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r9.anchor: فقال ثعلب : عندي غير هذا ، وهو الصواب عندي

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.claim: The discourse moves from day and night as models of developmental trials, to reassurance, promised better times, examples of past divine help, and duties arising from those favours.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p353/r2.anchor: Following is the sequence of the discourse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.claim: The future success promised to the Prophet is followed by reminders of earlier deliverance and spiritual blessing, then guidance to fulfil the duties those favours impose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p354/r1.anchor: At the end, he is guided to fulfil the obligations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r1.claim: Before prophethood the Prophet was neither in error nor fully guided in these questions, but earnestly sought truth in the seclusion of Ḥirāʾ.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r1.anchor: this state of his can neither be regarded as one of error nor of guidance. In precise words, this state of his reflects his effort to seek the truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r2.speaker: some books
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r2.claim: Some books describe Ḥanīfī seekers who yearned to worship God as He wished but lacked a way to know how; Islahi says this may also describe the Prophet’s state.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r2.anchor: Some books do describe the state of people

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r3.claim: The Qur’an describes this pre-revelation lack of scriptural knowledge as a state of not being aware, and revelation as the light that guides, in 42:52 and 12:3.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p360/r3.anchor: But we made this revelation a light whereby We guide

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r11.claim: One outward account says Muhammad lost his way in Mecca's passes as a child until his uncle Abu Talib guided him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r11.anchor: أي : ضللت في شعاب مكة ، فهدى إليك عمك أبا طالب في حال صباك

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r12.claim: Inwardly, being lost may mean bewilderment about God, then being guided by God to God; or lacking detailed religious rulings and being taught them.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r12.anchor: ويقال : ( ضالا ) فينا متحيرا . . فهديناك بنا إلينا

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r13.claim: Other readings say Muhammad found wandering peoples and guided them, sought divine intimacy, or was lost in love and guided by the light of nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r13.anchor: وقيل : ( ضالا ) في محبتنا ، فهديناك بنور القربة إلينا

QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r14.claim: Further readings say God revealed His love for Muhammad, his noble rank, or made him known after he had been concealed among Meccans.
QUSHAYRI:v3p429/r14.anchor: عن محبتي لك فعرفتك أني أحبك

FARRA:v3p273#2/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273#2/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273#2/r7.claim: “He found you lost” means among a misguided people; “found you needy” is also read in ʿAbd Allāh's codex as “destitute,” with the same sense.
FARRA:v3p273#2/r7.anchor: ووجدك ضالا فهدى (7) . يريد: في قوم ضلال فهداك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r8.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وفرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and others say God found the Prophet without the prophetic path and granted him prophethood and revelation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya's preferred sense is a near, temporary lack of direction while the Prophet searched and reflected, not the distant error of idolaters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r9.anchor: وهو الكون واقفا لا يميز المهيع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r10.claim: Al-Suddi says the Prophet remained upon his people's ways for forty years.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r10.anchor: وقال السدي: أقام على أمر قومه أربعين سنة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r11.speaker: الكلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi says God found the Prophet among a misguided people, as if one of them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r11.anchor: وقال الكلبي ووجدك في قوم ضلال فكأنك واحد منهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r12.claim: Against implications of idolatry, Ibn Atiyya says the Prophet never worshipped an idol, though he shared some customs and opposed many others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r12.anchor: ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يعبد صنما قط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet was lost as a young child in Mecca's ravines before being returned to Abd al-Muttalib.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عباس هو ضلاله وهو صغير في شعاب مكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r14.speaker: الترمذي وعبد العزيز بن يحيى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r14.claim: Al-Tirmidhi and Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya say dallan means unknown or obscure, until God made the Prophet known.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r14.anchor: وقال الترمذي وعبد العزيز بن يحيى: ضالا معناه خامل الذكر لا يعرفك الناس فهداهم إليك ربك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r15.claim: Ibn Atiyya favors a state of hesitation before revelation, supported by 42:52, where the Prophet had not known scripture or faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r15.anchor: والصواب أنه ضلال من توقف لا يدري كما قال عز وجل: ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r16.speaker: ثعلب عن أهل السنة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r16.claim: Thalab transmits from Ahl al-Sunna an interpretation involving the Prophet's marriage to his daughter in the pre-Islamic period.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p494/r16.anchor: قال ثعلب قال أهل السنة: هو تزويجه بنته في الجاهلية ونحوه،

STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.claim: The sūrah consoles the Prophet: it assures him God will not abandon him, recalls God's favors, and ends by urging care for the downtrodden and preaching the message.
STUDYQURAN:93:intro/r6.anchor: The main theme of the sūrah is consolation of the Prophet. It begins with an assertion that God would not abandon the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.claim: Linguistically, 94:1 follows the same pattern as 93:6, with the construction also implied in 93:7–8.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r4.anchor: Linguistically 94:1 follows the same pattern as 93:6, Did He not find thee . . ., which is also implied in 93:7–8.

STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.claim: Both sūrahs present God's bounties as relief: Sūrah 93 addresses external needs, Sūrah 94 spiritual relief; 94 recalls blessings, reassures, then commands exertion and turning to God.
STUDYQURAN:94:intro/r5.anchor: Thematically both sūrahs speak of the bounties that God has provided the Prophet Muhammad as relief for the difficulties that beset him

TABATABAI:93:3-7/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r9.claim: The Prophet's “being astray” means lacking guidance in himself considered apart from God's gift; like all creation he had no guidance except through God, even though divine guidance accompanied him from his beginning.
TABATABAI:93:3-7/r9.anchor: فلا هدى له صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ولا لأحد من الخلق إلا بالله سبحانه

THALABI:v10p225/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p225/r4.claim: God found Muhammad unaware of the state he would later reach and guided him to it.
THALABI:v10p225/r4.anchor: ووجدك ضالا عما أنت عليه اليوم، فهداك إلى الذي أنت عليه اليوم

THALABI:v10p225/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r5.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v10p225/r5.claim: He says Muhammad followed the ways of his people for forty years.
THALABI:v10p225/r5.anchor: قال السدي: كان على أمر قومه أربعين عاما

THALABI:v10p225/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r6.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v10p225/r6.claim: He says God found Muhammad among a misguided people and guided him to monotheism and prophethood; another view says He guided people through Muhammad.
THALABI:v10p225/r6.anchor: وقال الكلبي: وجدك في قوم ضلال فهداك إلى التوحيد، والنبوة

THALABI:v10p225/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r7.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب وابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p225/r7.claim: They say Muhammad lacked knowledge of prophetic teachings and the rulings of religious law, which God then taught him.
THALABI:v10p225/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب وابن كيسان: ووجدك ضالا عن معالم النبوة، وأحكام الشريعة غافلا عنها

THALABI:v10p225/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p225/r8.claim: Another explanation says Muhammad was lost in Mecca's ravines, and God guided him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
THALABI:v10p225/r8.anchor: وقيل: ضالا في شعاب مكة، فهداك الى جدك عبد المطلب

THALABI:v10p225/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r9.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي الضحى
THALABI:v10p225/r9.claim: He recounts that Muhammad got lost in Mecca as a small child and Abu Jahl returned him to his grandfather, making this a divine favor delivered through an enemy.
THALABI:v10p225/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ضل، وهو صبي صغير في شعاب مكة

THALABI:v10p225/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p225/r10.speaker: بشر بن سعيد عن أبيه
THALABI:v10p225/r10.claim: He recounts hearing Abd al-Muttalib circumambulate the Kaaba and ask God to return his grandson Muhammad, whom he had sent to search for lost camels.
THALABI:v10p225/r10.anchor: عن أبيه قال: حججت في الجاهلية، فإذا أنا برجل يطوف بالبيت، وهو يرتجز، ويقول:

THALABI:v10p226/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p226/r1.speaker: عبد المطلب
THALABI:v10p226/r1.claim: Abd al-Muttalib says Muhammad had never failed to return from an errand before and tells him that his distress at the delay will never leave him.
THALABI:v10p226/r1.anchor: ذهبت أبل له فأرسل ابن ابنه في طلبها، ولم يرسله في حاجة قط إلا جاء بها

THALABI:v10p226/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p226/r2.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v10p226/r2.claim: In a long account, Halima loses the child Muhammad in Mecca; an old man appeals to Hubal, but the idol and other idols fall and declare Muhammad will bring their destruction.
THALABI:v10p226/r2.anchor: وفي حديث كعب الأحبار، في مولد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وبدء أمره أن حليمة لما قضت حق الرضاع

THALABI:v10p227/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p227/r1.speaker: كعب الأحبار
THALABI:v10p227/r1.claim: The lost infant is found under a tree in the valley of Tihama after a voice announces that Muhammad's Lord will not abandon him; Abd al-Muttalib returns him safely to Mecca.
THALABI:v10p227/r1.anchor: فسمعنا مناديا ينادي من الهواء: معاشر الناس لا تضجوا، فإن لمحمد ربا لا يخذله ولا يضيعه

THALABI:v10p227/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p227/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v10p227/r2.claim: He says Satan diverted Muhammad's camel during a dark journey with Abu Talib, but Gabriel blew Satan to Abyssinia and returned the Prophet to the caravan.
THALABI:v10p227/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع عمه أبي طالب

THALABI:v10p229/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p229/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p229/r5.claim: The final kāf is omitted from fa-awā and the two parallel verbs to match the verse endings; the intended meaning remains clear.
THALABI:v10p229/r5.anchor: وحذف الكاف من قوله فآوى وأختيها لمشاكلة رؤوس الآي، ولأن المعنى معروف

BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r3.claim: Here ضال means lacking revealed laws and rulings that reason cannot discover and can only learn through transmission; it can also mean absent.
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r3.anchor: معنى الضلال فقدان الشرائع والخلو عن الأحكام التي لا يهتدي إليها العقول

BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r4.claim: Raghib says ضلال can mean any deviation, intentional or accidental and slight or great, so it applies to prophets and unbelievers in radically different senses.
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : يقال الضلال لكل عدود عن المنهج عمدا كان أو سهوا

BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r5.claim: God guided Muhammad to revealed law through scripture and taught him what he had not known; this favor began after orphanhood, when he already used sound judgment, worshipped no idol, and committed no indecency.
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r5.anchor: أي فهداك إلى مناهج الشرائع في تضاعيف ما أوحى إليك من الكتاب المبين

BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r6.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r6.claim: One interpretation makes the people the ones who were astray: God found the Prophet among them and guided them through him.
BURSEVI:v10p352#3/r6.anchor: وفي الأسئلة المقحمة معناه ووجدك بين ضالين فهداهم بك

BURSEVI:v10p353/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p353/r1.claim: A Sufi interpretation takes the Prophet's lostness as bewilderment in divine transcendence, then guidance as complete knowledge after sobriety following annihilation and ecstasy.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r1.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : أي متحيرا في تيه الألوهية

BURSEVI:v10p353/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p353/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v10p353/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that as a boy Muhammad was lost in Mecca's ravines; Abd al-Muttalib sought him in prayer, and Abu Jahl returned him, so God saved him through an enemy as with Moses and Pharaoh.
BURSEVI:v10p353/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ، إن النبي عليه السلام ضل في شعاب مكة

QASHANI:93:4-8/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:93:4-8/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:93:4-8/r4.claim: Being astray means being veiled from essential unity by attributes while in the realm of the spiritual father; God guided the Prophet Himself to the essence.
QASHANI:93:4-8/r4.anchor: عن التوحيد الذاتي عند كونك في عالم أبيك

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.claim: God sheltered the orphan through the Prophet, guided the lost through him, and enriched the needy through him; the Prophet was sought in pre-eternity and made an envoy to creation.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : معناه وجد اليتيم فآوى بك ، ووجد الضال فهدى بك

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r2.claim: God found the Prophet among a misguided people and guided them through him.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r2.anchor: وقال أيضا : وجدك بين قوم ضلال فهداهم بك

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.claim: Finding follows seeking; the Prophet was the sought beloved in the outward sense.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا : وجدك أي طلبت حتى وجدت ، والمطلوب هو المراد

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r4.claim: The Prophet was bewildered in witnessing God and sheltered with Him; poverty in seeing creatures was replaced by unveiling that made their observation unnecessary.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : الم يجدك متحيرا في مشاهدته فآواك إلى نفسه

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r5.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r5.claim: The natural self is poor because it lacks the way to gnosis.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r5.anchor: وقال سهل رحمه الله : وجد نفسك نفس الطبع فقيرة إلى سبيل المعرفة

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r7.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r7.claim: Jafar describes the Prophet as separated from God's love in pre-eternity until God granted him knowledge of Himself.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r7.anchor: قال جعفر : كنت ضالا عن محبتي لك في الأزل فمننت عليك بمعرفتي

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r8.claim: The word dall can mean lover: God found the Prophet longing for gnosis and bestowed it; 12:95 uses the related sense of enduring love.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : الضال في اللغة هو المحب أي : وجدك محبا للمعرفة

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r9.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r9.claim: The Prophet wandered among the subtleties of love and was gently guided to what he sought, the mystics' station of ecstatic bewilderment.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r9.anchor: وقال الجريري : وجدك مترددا في غوامض معاني المحبة فهداك بلطفه

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r11.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r11.claim: Being lost means seeking God's love and being guided to it.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم : وجدك ضالا أي طالبا لمحبته فهداك لها

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r12.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r12.claim: God showed the Prophet his own great station after he had been unaware of his worth.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r12.anchor: قال بعضهم : وجدك جاهلا بقدر نفسك فأشرفك على عظيم محلك

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r13.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r13.claim: God gave the Prophet a cup of nearness and affection for his lack of pure love, guiding him through it to gnosis.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r13.anchor: وجدك ضالا عن معنى محض المودة فسقاك كأسا من شراب القربة

SULAMI:v2p400#5/r14.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r14.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r14.claim: The Prophet was uncertain about the meaning of revelation and was guided to explain it, as 16:44 states.
SULAMI:v2p400#5/r14.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله في قوله : ﴿ ضالا ﴾ أي متحيرا في بيان الكتاب

SULAMI:v2p402/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.claim: The Prophet was hidden among Meccans and unrecognized as a prophet until God revealed him; through him the fortunate were guided and the wretched destroyed.
SULAMI:v2p402/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم : مستترا في أهل مكة لم يعرفك أحدا بالنبوة حتى اظهرك

SULAMI:v2p402/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r3.claim: Though outwardly like other people in condition and body, he was honored with special ascent, divine speech, vision, and direct witnessing.
SULAMI:v2p402/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ﴿ ووجدك ضالا ﴾ عائلا أي : طاهرا في الخلق

SULAMI:v2p402/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p402/r4.claim: Given the Prophet's supreme honor, ordinary categories of misguidance, guidance, poverty, wealth, weakness, strength, orphanhood, and shelter do not apply to him as they do to others.
SULAMI:v2p402/r4.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : إذا كان هو المعلاء في شرفه ، فأين الضلالة

SULAMI:v2p402/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r5.speaker: بندار بن الحسين
SULAMI:v2p402/r5.claim: He moved from reasoning by inference to direct recognition and was enriched by knowledge beyond proofs and witnesses.
SULAMI:v2p402/r5.anchor: وقال بندار بن الحسين : كنت قائما مقام الاستدلال فتعرفت إليك

SULAMI:v2p402/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p402/r6.claim: The Prophet was lost from formal conventions, not from gnosis.
SULAMI:v2p402/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : وجدك ضالا عن الرسوم لا عن المعرفة

SULAMI:v2p402/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.claim: Though his people did not know his worth, God singled him out with favors, revealed His hidden bounty, and made his standing among them manifest.
SULAMI:v2p402/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ومن ضاله في قومه لا يعرفون مقداره فخصه بخصائص بره

SULAMI:v2p402/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r10.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r10.claim: Being lost means seeking one's virtue without finding it until God guides one to it.
SULAMI:v2p402/r10.anchor: وقال بعضهم : في قوله : ﴿ ووجدك ضالا ﴾ أي طالبا لفضيلتك ضالا عنها

SULAMI:v2p402/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p402/r11.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p402/r11.claim: His prophethood was concealed among his family, then revealed; through him God guided some and misled others.
SULAMI:v2p402/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم : مستور النبوة في أهل بيتك فكشف عنك حتى عرفوك نبيا

SULAMI:v2p403/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p403/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p403/r1.claim: God taught the Prophet his worth and gave him a cup of pure affection, guiding him through love to knowledge of God.
SULAMI:v2p403/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : ﴿ ووجدك ضالا ﴾ تعرف قدر نفسك فأعلمك قدرك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.claim: In a discussion of Abu Talib's poetry, Ibn Amr says Muhammad was already a noble master; he explains orphanhood as losing both parents and poverty as the limited wealth then held by Arabs.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r1.anchor: من طريق موسى بن علي بن رباح عن أبيه رضي الله عنه قال : كنت عند مسلمة بن مخلد وعنده عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.claim: The Prophet recounts God's answer to his request for prophetic miracles: God reminded him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, enrichment, opening his chest, removing his burden, and raising his remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3443#2/r2.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ' سالت ربي مسالة وددت اني لم اكن سالته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.claim: The Prophet says that after he asked about miracles granted earlier prophets, God reminded him He had sheltered him as an orphan, guided and enriched him, opened his chest, and raised his remembrance.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سالت ربي مسالة وددت اني لم اكن سالته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.claim: A report says God answered Muhammad's comparison with Abraham and Moses by recalling his own blessings, including raised remembrance, and saying that He had chosen him as a close friend.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3445#3/r4.anchor: عن عدي بن ثابت قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' سالت ربي مسالة اني لم اكن سالته

TUSTARI:93:7/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:93:7/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:93:7/r1.claim: God found the Prophet unaware of his own worth and taught him his rank; He also led him from not knowing pure divine love to knowledge of God, granting prophethood and message as signs of nearness and unity.
TUSTARI:93:7/r1.anchor: أي وجدك لا تعرف قدر نفسك فعرفك قدرك، ووجدك ضالا عن معاني محض مودتك فسقاك من شراب مودته

TUSTARI:93:7/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:93:7/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:93:7/r2.claim: Another inward interpretation says God found the natural self impoverished and in need of the path to gnosis.
TUSTARI:93:7/r2.anchor: قال: وفيها وجه آخر: ووجدك نفسك نفس الطبع فقير إلى سبيل المعرفة.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.claim: Conflicting occasion reports suggest narrators lacked clarity; Ibn Ashur supposes the second revelation pause lasted about twelve days, to give the Prophet respite and build capacity for revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r1.anchor: فالذي نظنه أن احتباس الوحي في هذه المرة كان لمدة نحو من اثني عشر يوما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.claim: He reconciles reports by proposing a first pause of forty days, a second of roughly twelve, and the present surah as the third revelation, when practice of arduous work develops; this also reconciles reports about al-Muddaththir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r2.anchor: فيكون نزول سورة الضحى هو النزول الثالث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.claim: The object of qalaa is omitted because waddaka makes it clear, a verbal ellipsis also seen in the following verbs awa, hada, and aghna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p396/r3.anchor: وحذف مفعول { قلى } لدلالة { ودعك } عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.claim: The childhood-care account proves the promise is certain: God's steady care from the Prophet's beginnings cannot be coincidence, and reassures believers while warning opponents that the promise will occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r4.anchor: استئناف مسوق مساق الدليل على تحقق الوعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.claim: The rhetorical question expects assent; wajada means encountered, takes one object, and yatiim, dallan, and aa'il are circumstantial states in an image of aid given to someone in distress.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p398/r5.anchor: والاستفهام تقريري ، وفعل { يجدك } مضارع وجد بمعنى ألفى وصادف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.claim: The objects of awa, hada, and aghna are omitted because the preceding second-person pronoun supplies them; the ellipsis is concise and preserves the verse endings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p400/r2.anchor: وحذفت مفاعيل { فآوى } ، { فهدى } ، { فأغنى } للعلم بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور منهم الحسن والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r1.claim: The Prophet lacked knowledge of prophetic signs and religious rulings, and God guided him to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r1.anchor: ضالا عن معالم النبوة وأحكام الشريعة فهداك إليها قاله الجمهور منهم الحسن والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r2.claim: As a small child, the Prophet became lost in Mecca's ravines, and God returned him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r2.anchor: أنه ضل وهو صبي صغير في شعاب مكة فرده الله إلى جده عبد المطلب رواه أبو الضحى عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r3.claim: On a journey with Khadija's servant Maysara, Satan diverted the Prophet's camel; Gabriel drove Satan away and returned the caravan to its route.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r3.anchor: أخذ إبليس بزمام ناقته فعدل به عن الطريق فجاء جبريل فنفخ إبليس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r4.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r4.claim: God found the Prophet among a misguided people and guided him to monotheism and prophethood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r4.anchor: ووجدك في قوم ضلال فهداك للتوحيد والنبوة قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r5.speaker: ثعلب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r5.claim: He was forgetful, then God guided him to remembrance, as in the rule that one witness reminds the other.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r5.anchor: ووجدك نسيا فهداك إلى الذكر ومثله ﴿ أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى ﴾ [ البقرة 282 ] قاله ثعلب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r6.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى ومحمد بن علي الترمذي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r6.claim: The Prophet had been obscure and unknown, so God guided people to him until they recognized him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p158#2/r6.anchor: ووجدك خاملا لاتذكر ولا تعرف فهدى الناس إليك حتى عرفوك قاله عبد العزيز بن يحيى ومحمد بن علي الترمذي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r1.claim: God guided Muhammad, as in the revelation that he did not know Scripture or faith before the Spirit was made a light guiding him to a straight path.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r1.anchor: وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r2.claim: Some say Muhammad became lost in Mecca's mountain passes as a child and then returned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r2.anchor: ومنهم من قال [إن] (3) المراد بهذا أنه، عليه السلام، ضل في شعاب مكة وهو صغير، ثم رجع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r3.speaker: البغوي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r3.claim: A report cited by al-Baghawi says Satan diverted Muhammad's camel on the night road to Syria with his uncle; Gabriel blew Satan toward Abyssinia and redirected the mount.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r3.anchor: فجاء جبريل، فنفخ إبليس نفخة ذهب منها إلى الحبشة، ثم عدل بالراحلة إلى الطريق. حكاهما البغوي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.claim: Qatada says orphanhood, being guided, and being provided for were the Prophet's circumstances before God sent him as a messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p426/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك ضالا فهدى ووجدك عائلا فأغنى} قال: كانت هذه منازل الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يبعثه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet recounting God's reminders that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, enriched him, expanded his chest, and raised his remembrance; he affirms each gift.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p430/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أكن سألته

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.claim: One explanation for the pause in revelation is that a puppy was in the Prophet's house; Gabriel said angels do not enter a house containing a dog or image.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r1.anchor: وقيل: سبب احتباسه كون جرو في بيته، فلما نزل جبريل سأله عن تأخيره

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.claim: Another report links the revelation to the Prophet's words on the Night Journey about David receiving iron and Abraham receiving fire.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r2.anchor: وقيل: قال ليلة المعراج: سخرت الحديد لداود، والنار لإبراهيم

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.claim: The Prophet asked why Solomon and others received great gifts; God reminded him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him, and he affirmed each reminder.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس، عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: سألت ربي مسألة

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj gives twelve days as the duration of the revelation pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r5.anchor: فقيل: اثنا عشر يوما، عن ابن جريج.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives fifteen days as the duration of the revelation pause.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r6.anchor: وقيل: خمسة عشر يوما، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r7.claim: Another report gives twenty-five days without naming its transmitter.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r8.claim: Muqātil gives forty days as the duration of the revelation pause.

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.claim: A report says the Prophet told Gabriel he had missed him; Gabriel replied that he missed him more, but descends only when commanded by his Lord.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r9.anchor: قال له النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: قد اشتقت إليك، فقال: وأنا أشد شوقا إليك

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.claim: If a pause is established, it should be explained as serving a benefit; neglecting the formula of exception taught believers but could not delay their interests.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r10.anchor: والصحيح إن ثبت التأخير أن يقال: إنه تأخير للمصلحة

JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.claim: Stories that the Prophet asked for gifts during or after the Night Journey are unsound: he asks only with permission, and a permitted request must be answered.
JISHUMI:v10p7452/r11.anchor: فأما ما ذكروا من سؤاله ليلة المعراج وبعده فغير صحيح

JISHUMI:v10p7457/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r1.claim: One account says ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib sent the child Muḥammad to seek camels; he went missing, and the grandfather prayed until the boy returned with the herd.
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r1.anchor: بعث به جده عبد المطلب في طلب إبل، فاحتبس عنه، وهو صبي

JISHUMI:v10p7457/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r2.speaker: كعب
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r2.claim: In a long story, Ḥalīma lost the child near Mecca; an old man directed her to Hubal, but the idols fell and a voice foretold their destruction by Muḥammad; ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib later found him.
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r2.anchor: فذهب عبد المطلب، وجاء به في حديث طويل، عن كعب.

JISHUMI:v10p7457/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r3.claim: On a Syria caravan journey with Abū Ṭālib, Satan diverted the Prophet's camel, Gabriel blew Satan toward Abyssinia and returned the camel; if the report is sound, an unbeliever diverted him and a believer restored him.
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r3.anchor: جاء إبليس فأخذ بزمام الناقة، فعدل به عن الطريق، فجاء جبريل

JISHUMI:v10p7457/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r4.claim: Another view takes ḍāll as not knowing the way when Gabriel left him on the Night Journey, after which Gabriel guided him to the Lote or Throne area.
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r4.anchor: وجدك ضالا ليلة المعراج لا تعرف الطريق حين انصرف جبريل

JISHUMI:v10p7457/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r5.claim: Because Arabs call a solitary desert tree a ḍālla and use it to find a road, this view reads the verse as saying Muḥammad was unique among prophets and guided humanity to truth.
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن العرب تسمي الشجرة الفريدة في فلاة ضالة، فيهتدون بها إلى الطريق

JISHUMI:v10p7457/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r6.claim: Another interpretation says he was obscure and unknown, then God made him known and honored among people, guiding them through him.
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r6.anchor: وقيل: وجدك خاملا لا تذكر ولا تعرف، فعرفك إلى الناس

JISHUMI:v10p7457/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r7.claim: The author prefers Abū ʿAlī's earlier explanation and regards the other readings as forced or unsupported specifications.
JISHUMI:v10p7457/r7.anchor: وأحسن ما قيل فيه ما قال أبو علي، وبدأنا به وما تعداه

JISHUMI:v10p7459/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7459/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7459/r16.claim: One should not simply call the Prophet astray, despite the Qur'anic wording, because that could suggest deviation from religion.
JISHUMI:v10p7459/r16.anchor: قلنا: لا، وإن ورد به القرآن؛ لأنه يوهم الضلال عن الدين.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r5.claim: Being lost means lacking knowledge of revealed laws, as in 42:52, rather than being a disbeliever.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r5.anchor: ضالا } معناه الضلال عن علم الشرائع وما طريقة السمع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r6.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r6.claim: Other accounts say he was lost as a boy in Mecca, lost by Halima after weaning, or lost on the Syrian road with Abu Talib.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : ضل في صباه في بعض شعاب مكة ، فرده أبو جهل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r7.claim: Guidance means teaching him Qur'an and revealed law, or removing mistaken assumptions others had about him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r7.anchor: فهداك : فعرفك القرآن والشرائع . أو فأزال ضلالك عن جدك زعمك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r8.claim: If saying he followed his people for forty years means lacking revealed knowledge, that is acceptable; if it means their disbelief, it is false, since prophets are protected from sin and unbelief.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p772#2/r8.anchor: ومن قال : كان على أمر قومه أربعين سنة ، فإن أراد أنه كان على خلوهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r1.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r1.claim: He read the verse with a masculine active verb: He found you astray, then you found guidance through Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p294/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ووجدك ضال فهدي , أي وجدك الضال

MUQATIL:93:7-11/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:93:7-11/r1.speaker: جبريل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:93:7-11/r1.claim: Gabriel glosses finding Muhammad astray as his being without guidance, then God guided him to His religion; the Prophet responds that his Lord showed him favor and is worthy of praise, and repeats the response when told God found him poor and enriched him.
MUQATIL:93:7-11/r1.anchor: فقال جبريل، عليه السلام: { ووجدك ضآلا } على الدلالة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#4/r1.claim: The Prophet was not yet aware of the prophetic way, revealed law, or matters known through transmitted revelation; God taught him the laws and Qur'an.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ ووجدك ضالا ﴾ أ ى غير عالم ولا واقف على معالم النبوه وأحكام الشريعة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#4/r2.claim: Another report says he lost the road to Syria while traveling with Abu Talib and was returned to the caravan; the verse cannot mean that he left truth or committed idolatry, for he was protected from that from childhood until revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p345#4/r2.anchor: وقيل ضل فى طريق الشام حين خرج به أبو طالب فرده إلى القافلة

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r1.claim: Dall means unaware of what was intended for him in prophethood, and God guided him; here it means forgetfulness or unawareness, as in 20:52 and 12:3.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r1.anchor: أي غافلا عما يراد بك من أمر النبوة، فهداك: أي أرشدك. والضلال هنا بمعنى الغفلة

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r2.speaker: الضحاك، شهر بن حوشب
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r2.claim: They say Muhammad did not yet know the Qur’an and religious laws, and God guided him to them, as at 42:52.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: { ضآلا } لم تكن تدري القرآن والشرائع، فهداك الله إلى القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r3.speaker: الكلبي، الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r3.claim: They say the Prophet found his people astray and God guided them through him.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: { ووجدك ضآلا } أي في قوم ضلال، فهداهم الله بك

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r4.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r4.claim: Al-Suddi similarly takes the lost people as the Prophet’s community, whom he was guided to direct.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r4.anchor: وعن السدي نحوه أي ووجد قومك في ضلال، فهداك إلى إرشادهم

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that he was uncertain about migration, and God guided him to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r5.anchor: وقيل: «ووجدك ضالا» عن الهجرة، فهداك إليها

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r6.claim: Another view says he forgot to say “if God wills” when asked about the sleepers, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; God reminded him, as in 2:282.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r6.anchor: وقيل: «ضالا» أي ناسيا شأن الاستثناء حين سئلت

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r7.claim: Another view says he sought the direction of prayer and God guided him to it, as at 2:144.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r7.anchor: وقيل: ووجدك طالبا للقبلة فهداك إليها

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r8.claim: Because a person who is lost is a seeker, dall can mean “seeking.”
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r8.anchor: ويكون الضلال بمعنى الطلب لأن الضال طالب

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r9.claim: Another view says he was perplexed about explaining revelation and God guided him; dall then means confused.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r9.anchor: وقيل: ووجدك متحيرا عن بيان ما نزل عليك، فهداك إليه فيكون الضلال بمعنى التحير

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r10.claim: Another view takes dall to mean lost or neglected among his people until God guided him.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r10.anchor: وقيل: ووجدك ضائعا في قومك فهداك إليه ويكون الضلال بمعنى الضياع

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r11.claim: Another view says he loved guidance and God led him to it; the usage of 12:95 means love or attachment.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r11.anchor: وقيل: ووجدك محبا للهداية، فهداك إليها ويكون الضلال بمعنى المحبة

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r12.claim: Poetry uses dall for love or attachment.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r12.anchor: قال الشاعر: هذا الضلال أشاب مني المفرقا والعارضين ولم أكن متحققا

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad became lost in Mecca’s ravines as a child and Abu Jahl returned him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r13.anchor: وقيل: «ضالا» في شعاب مكة، فهداك وردك إلى جدك عبد المطلب

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r14.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says Satan led the camel off course during a dark journey with Abu Talib; Gabriel drove Satan to India and returned them to the caravan.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r14.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: خرج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مع عمه أبي طالب في سفر، فأخذ إبليس بزمام الناقة في ليلة ظلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r15.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r15.claim: Kaab narrates that while Halima returned the child at Mecca, a sudden noise accompanied his disappearance; the story continues in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7/r15.anchor: وقال كعب: إن حليمة لما قضت حق الرضاع، جاءت برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لترده على عبد المطلب

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r1.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r1.claim: In Kaab’s story, the old man sends Halima to the idol, which falls and declares fear of Muhammad; he tells her to search patiently.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r1.anchor: ثم طاف الشيخ بالصنم، وقبل رأسه وقال: يا رب، لم تزل منتك على قريش

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r2.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r2.claim: Abd al-Muttalib searches all Mecca and prays a poem asking God to return Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r2.anchor: فطاف عبد المطلب بالكعبة سبعا، وتضرع إلى الله أن يرده، وقال: يا رب رد ولدي محمدا

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r3.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r3.claim: A heavenly voice directs the searchers to Muhammad under a samara tree in Wadi Tihama, where they find him.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r3.anchor: فسمعوا مناديا ينادي من السماء: معاشر الناس لا تضجوا، فإن لمحمد ربا لا يخذله ولا يضيعه

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r4.claim: Another view says Muhammad lost the path during the Night Journey after Gabriel left, and God guided him to the Lote Tree of the Throne.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: «ووجدك ضالا» ليلة المعراج، حين انصرف عنك جبريل

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq and others say Muhammad loved Abu Talib, but God redirected his love toward the Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق وغيره: «ووجدك ضالا»: تحب أبا طالب

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r6.speaker: بسام بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r6.claim: Bassam ibn Abd Allah interprets it as Muhammad not knowing himself until God made him know himself and his condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r6.anchor: وقال بسام بن عبد الله: «ووجدك ضالا» بنفسك لا تدري من أنت

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r7.speaker: الجنيدي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r7.claim: Al-Junayd says Muhammad was perplexed about explaining the Book and God taught him clarity, linked to 16:44 and 16:64.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r7.anchor: وقال الجنيدي: ووجدك متحيرا في بيان الكتاب، فعلمك البيان بيانه

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r8.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r8.claim: Some theologians compare a lone desert tree, called dall because it guides travelers, to Muhammad alone in faith whose guidance led creation to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r8.anchor: إذا وجدت العرب شجرة منفردة في فلاة من الأرض، لا شجر معها، سموها ضالة

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls the interpretations sound and the final, unifying interpretation most appealing because it gathers the metaphorical explanations.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r9.anchor: قلت: هذه الأقوال كلها حسان، ثم منها ما هو معنوي، ومنها ما هو حسي. والقول الأخير أعجب إلي لأنه يجمع الأقوال المعنوية

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r10.claim: Some say Muhammad outwardly followed his people’s customs for forty years without openly opposing them, but this does not mean he committed idolatry.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r10.anchor: وقال قوم: إنه كان على جملة ما كان القوم عليه، لا يظهر لهم خلافا على ظاهر الحال فأما الشرك فلا يظن به

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r11.speaker: الكلبي، السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi take “lost” literally as unbelief before guidance; al-Qurtubi says this was addressed and refuted at al-Shura.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r11.anchor: وقال الكلبي والسدي: هذا على ظاهره أي وجدك كافرا والقوم كفار فهداك

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r12.claim: Another view says Muhammad was submerged among the polytheists, then distinguished from them.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: وجدك مغمورا بأهل الشرك، فميزك عنهم

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r1.claim: Dall can mean submerged into the earth and no longer distinguishable, as in 32:10 about being lost in the earth at burial.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r1.anchor: أي لحقنا بالتراب عند الدفن، حتى كأنا لا نتميز من جملته

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r2.claim: Al-Hasan’s explanatory reading says “He found you lost, then you were guided,” meaning the people were guided through him.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r2.anchor: وفي قراءة الحسن «ووجدك ضال فهدى» أي وجدك الضال فاهتدى بك

QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r3.claim: Another view says the people could not locate or recognize Muhammad’s worth, until God guided them to him through the Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:93:7#3/r3.anchor: وقيل: «ووجدك ضالا» لا يهتدي إليك قومك، ولا يعرفون قدرك

QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r2.claim: Raised amid confused pagan beliefs and practices, the Prophet found no reassuring way in paganism or among followers of Moses and Jesus who had altered their faith; God guided him through revelation and its way.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r2.anchor: ثم هداك الله بالأمر الذي أوحي به إليك ، وبالمنهج الذي يصلك به

QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r3.claim: Guidance from doctrinal confusion is the greatest favor, bringing incomparable rest and calm; the verse reassured the Prophet during interrupted revelation, pagan gloating, and the loneliness of separation from his beloved Lord.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:7/r3.anchor: والهداية من حيرة العقيدة وضلال الشعاب فيها هي المنة الكبرى

QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r2.claim: Raised amid confused pagan beliefs and practices, the Prophet found no reassuring way in paganism or among followers of Moses and Jesus who had altered their faith; God guided him through revelation and its way.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r2.anchor: ثم هداك الله بالأمر الذي أوحي به إليك ، وبالمنهج الذي يصلك به

QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r3.claim: Guidance from doctrinal confusion is the greatest favor, bringing incomparable rest and calm; the verse reassured the Prophet during interrupted revelation, pagan gloating, and the loneliness of separation from his beloved Lord.
QUTB-ZILAL:93:8/r3.anchor: والهداية من حيرة العقيدة وضلال الشعاب فيها هي المنة الكبرى

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.claim: Repaying benefaction is a lifelong, weightier debt than a financial loan; since God's gifts cannot be repaid, the servant should extend the same care to orphans and needy seekers and remember God's favor.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r6.anchor: فكأن العبد يقول : إلهي أخرجتني من العدم إلى الوجود بشرا سويا ، طاهر الظاهر نجس الباطن

RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.claim: The practical answer to unrepayable divine gifts is to shelter orphans, guide and aid God's servants, and continually remember that even this service depends on God's help.
RAZI-FULL:v31p194#3/r7.anchor: فيقول تعالى الطريق إلى ذلك أن تفعل في حق عبيدي ما فعلته في حقك ، كنت يتيما فآويتك

RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says Muhammad was among a misguided people and God guided him to monotheism; al-Suddi says he followed his people's religion for forty years; Mujahid says he lacked guidance to his religion.
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي : { ووجدك ضالا } يعني كافرا في قوم ضلال فهداك للتوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r2.claim: Those alleging prior unbelief cite 42:52, 12:3, and 39:65 as support for ignorance of revelation and the conditional warning against association.
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r2.anchor: ما كنت تدرى ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان } ( الشورى : 52 ) وقوله : { وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r3.claim: The majority of scholars agree that the Prophet never disbelieved in God, even for an instant.
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r3.anchor: وأما الجمهور من العلماء فقد اتفقوا على أنه عليه السلام ما كفر بالله لحظة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r4.claim: The Mu'tazila deem even a possible period of unbelief rationally impermissible because it would repel people from the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r4.anchor: ثم قالت المعتزلة : هذا غير جائز عقلا لما فيه من التنفير

RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r5.claim: The author's theological school allows that possibility in reason, but says scriptural evidence shows it did not occur, citing the declaration that the Prophet neither strayed nor erred.
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r5.anchor: إلا أن الدليل السمعي قام على أن هذا الجائز لم يقع وهو قوله تعالى : { ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى }

RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r6.claim: They interpret the phrase as ignorance of divine favor and the religious law, which God then taught through revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r6.anchor: أحدها : ما روي عن ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب : { ووجدك ضالا } عن معالم النعمة

RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r7.claim: One account says Halima lost the child while returning him to his grandfather; at Hubal the idols fell and a voice foretold their destruction by him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r7.anchor: ضل عن مرضعته حليمة حين أرادت أن ترده إلى جده حتى دخلت إلى هبل وشكت ذلك إليه فتساقطت الأصنام

RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits a report attributed to the Prophet that, as a lost and hungry boy separated from his grandfather, God guided him back.
RAZI-FULL:v31p195#2/r8.anchor: وثالثها : ما روي مرفوعا أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( ضللت عن جدي عبد المطلب وأنا صبي ضائع

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God returned Muhammad to his grandfather through an enemy, just as He preserved Moses through an enemy.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : رده الله إلى جده بيد عدوه كما فعل بموسى حين حفظه على يد عدوه

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r2.claim: Another account says a disbeliever leading his camel lost Muhammad on a journey with Khadija's servant Maysara; Gabriel appeared as a man and guided him to the caravan.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r2.anchor: ورابعها : أنه عليه السلام لما خرج مع غلام خديجة ميسرة أخذ كافر بزمام بعيره حتى ضل ،

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r3.claim: It is also said that Abu Talib took Muhammad to Syria, where he lost the route and God guided him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن أبا طالب خرج به إلى الشأم فضل عن الطريق فهداه الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r4.claim: Using the idiom of water submerged in milk, the verse can mean Muhammad was overwhelmed among Meccan unbelievers until God strengthened him to manifest the faith.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r4.anchor: وخامسها : يقال : ضل الماء في اللبل إذا صار مغمورا ، فمعنى الآية كنت مغمورا بين الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r5.claim: A solitary tree in the wilderness is called ḍāllah: Muhammad was the lone tree bearing faith and knowledge in a barren land, and through him God guided people; this resembles the saying that wisdom is the believer's lost property.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r5.anchor: وسادسها : العرب تسمي الشجرة الفريدة في الفلاة ضالة ، كأنه تعالى يقول : كانت تلك البلاد

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r6.claim: Another reading is that as a child he was without knowledge of God, like all people at birth; ḍāll here means devoid of knowledge, not holding a false belief.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r6.anchor: فخلق فيك العقل والهداية والمعرفة / والمراد من الضال الخالي عن العلم لا الموصوف بالاعتقاد الخطأ

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r7.claim: He may have been unaware of his future prophethood, which neither he expected nor the Jews and Christians thought could belong outside Israel.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r7.anchor: وثامنها : كنت ضالا عن النبوة ما كنت تطمع في ذلك ولا خطر شيء من ذلك في قلبك

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r8.claim: A singular address may refer to Muhammad's people: they were astray, and God guided them through him and his law.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r8.anchor: وتاسعها : أنه قد يخاطب السيد ، ويكون المراد قومه فقوله : { ووجدك ضالا } أي وجد قومك ضلالا

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r9.claim: It may mean he stood apart from the misguided; God guided him to mix with them and call them to the manifest religion.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r9.anchor: وعاشرها : وجدك ضالا عن الضالين منفردا عنهم مجانبا لدينهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r10.claim: Another interpretation concerns his wish to leave Quraysh but inability to depart without permission; God guided the emigration, the route to Umm Ma'bad, and the events with Suraqa.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r10.anchor: الحادي عشر : وجدك ضالا عن الهجرة ، متحيرا في يد قريش متمنيا فراقهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r11.claim: He desired the Kaaba as qibla but did not know if it would be granted, then God directed him to the desired prayer direction.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r11.anchor: الثاني عشر : ضالا عن القبلة ، فإنه كان يتمنى أن تجعل الكعبة قبلة له

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r12.claim: At Gabriel's first appearance, Muhammad did not know who he was and was frightened; God guided him until he recognized Gabriel.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r12.anchor: الثالث عشر : أنه حين ظهرها له جبريل عليه السلام في أول أمره ما كان يعرف أهو جبريل أم لا

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r13.claim: Ḍalāl can mean love, as in Jacob's deep love for Joseph; God guided Muhammad to laws by which he could serve his beloved Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r13.anchor: الرابع عشر : الضلال بمعنى المحبة كما في قوله : { إنك لفى ضلالك القديم } ( يوسف : 95 ) أي محبتك

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r14.claim: He lacked worldly and commercial know-how, then God guided him to profitable trade that drew Khadija's interest; his attention had been devoted to religion.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r14.anchor: الخامس عشر : ضالا عن أمور الدنيا لا تعرف التجارة ونحوها ، ثم هديتك حتى ربحت تجارتك

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r15.claim: The verse can mean that he was lost and powerless among people who mistreated and rejected him, until God made him their commander.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r15.anchor: السادس عشر : { ووجدك ضالا } أي ضائعا في قومك ؛ كانوا يؤذونك ، ولا يرضون بك رعية

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r16.claim: It may refer to not knowing the route through the heavens until God guided him on the night journey and ascension.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r16.anchor: السابع عشر : كنت ضالا ما كنت تهتدي على طريق السموات فهديتك إذ عرجت بك إلى السموات

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r17.claim: By analogy with a woman being led into error, ḍalāl can mean forgetting: in awe on the night journey he forgot words of praise until taught to say he could not enumerate God's praise.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r17.anchor: الثامن عشر : ووجدك ضالا أي ناسيا لقوله تعالى : { أن تضل إحداهما } ( البقرة : 282 )

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r18.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r18.claim: Ali transmits the Prophet's account that God twice prevented him from joining pre-Islamic nighttime entertainment; he fell asleep until sunlight, and afterward never intended evil until his mission.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r18.anchor: العشرون : روى علي عليه السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( ما هممت بشيء مما كان

RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r19.claim: The continuation gives the Prophet's story of twice being prevented by sleep from joining young men at a wedding celebration, after which he never intended evil.
RAZI-FULL:v31p196/r19.anchor: فما أيقظني إلا مس الشمس ، قال فجئت صاحبي ، فقال ما فعلت ؟

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.claim: Mentioning these circumstances keeps the Prophet mindful of them and prevents self-admiration.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r8.anchor: الحكمة أن لا ينسى نفسه فيقع في العجب

RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.claim: The judge criticizes a report in which the Prophet asks why others received special favors: prophets only ask with permission, and God's reply sounds reproachful.
RAZI-FULL:v31p198/r9.anchor: فهل يصح هذا الحديث قلنا : طعن القاضي في هذا الخبر فقال : إن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يسألون مثل ذلك

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r3.speaker: al-Baghawī
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r3.claim: One reading is that God taught Muhammad his true nature as God's messenger.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r3.anchor: This verse can be taken as reference to God’s teaching Muhammad his true nature as a messenger of God

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r4.claim: A literal reading says Muhammad was astray until God guided him to monotheism and prophethood.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r4.anchor: Some understand this verse literally to mean that Muhammad had been astray and that God guided him to belief in the Oneness of God

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r5.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r5.claim: Others say the Prophet lacked a revealed law or rite, unknown to his people, without having strayed from monotheistic belief.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r5.anchor: For others, this verse means that the Prophet had strayed in the sense that he did not follow a revealed law or rite

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r6.claim: A related reading is that Muhammad believed in God's Oneness but had neither scripture nor direct guidance before the Quran was revealed.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r6.anchor: although he believed in the Oneness of God, he had no scripture and no direct guidance until the Quran was revealed

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r7.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r7.claim: To avoid religious implications, some take the verse to refer to Muhammad being lost in Makkah's streets until Gabriel guided him.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r7.anchor: Some try to avoid the implication that the Prophet could have been astray in any religious or spiritual sense

STUDYQURAN:93:5/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r8.speaker: still others
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r8.claim: Another report says the Prophet's mount strayed from the road during a journey and Gabriel returned him to the way.
STUDYQURAN:93:5/r8.anchor: Still others see it as a reference to a time when the Prophet was on a journey, his mount strayed from the road

TAB:93:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:7/r2.speaker: author
TAB:93:7/r2.claim: God found Muhammad in a condition unlike his present state and guided him; the passage recounts divine blessings to the Prophet.
TAB:93:7/r2.anchor: وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالاً فَهَدَى ووجدك على غير الذي أنت عليه اليوم

TAB:93:7/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:7/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB:93:7/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Muhammad followed the way of his people for forty years before guidance.
TAB:93:7/r3.anchor: عن السديّ وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالاً قال :  كان على أمر قومه أربعين عاما

TAB:93:7/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:7/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:93:7/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation is that God found Muhammad among a misguided people and guided him.
TAB:93:7/r4.anchor: وقيل :  عُنِي بذلك :  ووجدك في قوم ضُلاّل فهداك

TAB:93:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:8/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB:93:8/r4.claim: Qatada calls orphanhood, being astray, and poverty the conditions of the Messenger before God sent him.
TAB:93:8/r4.anchor: عن قتادة أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيما فآوَى وَوَجَدَك ضَالاّ فَهَدَى وَوَجَدَكَ عائِلاً فأغْنَى قال :  كانت هذه منازل رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v24p489/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says Muḥammad followed his people's way for forty years before revelation.
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r2.anchor: عن السدي، {ووجدك ضالا} [الضحى: 7] قال: كان على أمر قومه أربعين عاما

TAB-FULL:v24p489/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that God found Muḥammad among a people in error and guided him.
TAB-FULL:v24p489/r3.anchor: وقيل: عني بذلك: ووجدك في قوم ضلال فهداك

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r1.claim: Moses’ ‘I was among the astray’ means he had not yet received the guidance of prophethood; this is compared with the Prophet’s earlier lack of knowledge of scripture and faith.
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r1.anchor: ومن هذا الباب قول موسى على ما حكى الله عنه فعلتها إذا وأنا من الضالين

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes ضالّ as lacking knowledge, as in the verse about one woman forgetting and the other reminding her.
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r2.anchor: وقيل المعنى وجدك ضالا بين الناس لا يعرفون حقك

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r3.claim: The verse ‘you were among the unaware’ before revelation supports the interpretation of ضالّ as lacking prior knowledge.
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r3.anchor: ويؤيده قوله وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r4.claim: One view says the Prophet was lost among people who did not know his worth, and God guided them to recognize him.
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r4.anchor: وقيل إنه إشارة إلى ضلاله في طريق مكة

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r5.claim: A report says he was lost on the road to Mecca when Halima brought him from the desert to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r6.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r6.claim: Another report says he was lost in Mecca’s ravines as a child.
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r6.anchor: وقيل إشارة إلى ما روي من ضلاله في شعاب مكة صغيرا

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r7.claim: A further report places the incident on his journey to Syria with his uncle Abu Talib, in Maysara Khadija’s servant’s caravan.
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r7.anchor: في مسيره إلى الشام مع عمه أبي طالب في قافلة ميسرة غلام خديجة

TABATABAI:93:8-11/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r8.claim: The road, ravines, and caravan interpretations, along with similar suggestions, are manifestly weak.
TABATABAI:93:8-11/r8.anchor: وقيل غير ذلك وهي وجوه ضعيفة ظاهرة الضعف

ZAJJAJ:v5p339#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p339#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p339#2/r1.claim: Ḍāll means the Prophet did not yet know the Qur'an or religious laws, so God guided him to them; 42:52 supports this explanation.
ZAJJAJ:v5p339#2/r1.anchor: أنه لم يكن يدري القرآن ولا الشرائع فهداه الله إلى القرآن وشرائع الإسلام

ZAJJAJ:v5p339#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p339#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p339#2/r2.claim: Another group says he remained upon his people's way for forty years.
ZAJJAJ:v5p339#2/r2.anchor: وقال قوم: كان على أمر قومه أربعين سنة (1).

TABRISI:93:5-7/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:5-7/r8.speaker: الحسن، الضحاك، الجبائي
TABRISI:93:5-7/r8.claim: They interpret “astray” as not yet knowing the prophethood and sacred law, then being guided to them; this means lack of knowledge, as in 12:3 and 2:282.
TABRISI:93:5-7/r8.anchor: وجدك ضالا عما أنت عليه الآن من النبوة والشريعة أي كنت غافلا عنهما فهداك إليهما

TABRISI:93:8/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:8/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:93:8/r1.claim: Abū Muslim says “astray” means not knowing how to earn a livelihood, then being guided to its means; a Prophetic saying relates his provision to jihad.
TABRISI:93:8/r1.anchor: وجدك متحيرا لا تعرف وجوه معاشك فهداك إلى وجوه معاشك

TABRISI:93:8/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:8/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:8/r2.claim: Another reading says God found him unaware of the truth and guided him through reason, proofs, and divine favor to know God's attributes amid idolatry.
TABRISI:93:8/r2.anchor: وجدك لا تعرف الحق فهداك إليه بإتمام العقل ونصب الأدلة والإلطاف

TABRISI:93:8/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:8/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:93:8/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that young Muḥammad became lost in Meccan ravines; Abū Jahl returned him to his grandfather.
TABRISI:93:8/r3.anchor: ضل في شعاب مكة وهو صغير فرآه أبو جهل ورده إلى جده عبد المطلب

TABRISI:93:8/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:8/r4.speaker: كعب
TABRISI:93:8/r4.claim: A long account says Ḥalīma lost the child while returning him; after the idols failed, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib prayed and recovered him under a tree.
TABRISI:93:8/r4.anchor: لما أرضعته مدة وقضت حق الرضاع ثم أرادت رده على جده جاءت به

TABRISI:93:8/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:8/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TABRISI:93:8/r5.claim: Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib says Satan diverted the Prophet's camel during a night journey with Abū Ṭālib, but Gabriel drove Satan away and returned him to the caravan.
TABRISI:93:8/r5.anchor: خرج مع عمه أبي طالب في ميسرة غلام خديجة فبينما هو راكب ذات ليلة ظلماء

TABRISI:93:8/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:8/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:93:8/r6.claim: Alternatively, the Prophet was obscure among people who did not recognize his merit; God made him known, honored, and believed.
TABRISI:93:8/r6.anchor: كنت خاملا لا تذكر ولا تعرف فعرفك الله الناس حتى عرفوك وعظموك

TABRISI:93:10-11/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:93:10-11/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:93:10-11/r6.claim: The petitioner may be someone seeking knowledge; teach him the religious laws as God taught you when you did not know them, continuing the preceding reference to guidance.
TABRISI:93:10-11/r6.anchor: المراد بالسائل طلب العلم وهو متصل بقوله

THALABI:v10p228/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p228/r1.claim: One explanation places the verse at the Night Journey: Gabriel left the Prophet unsure of the route, and God guided him to the Lote Tree at the Throne.
THALABI:v10p228/r1.anchor: وقيل: وجدك ضالا ليلة المعراج حين انصرف عنك جبرائيل لا تعرف الطريق، فهداك إلى ساق العرش

THALABI:v10p228/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r2.speaker: بعض أهل الكلام
THALABI:v10p228/r2.claim: They explain that an isolated tree in open country is called ḍālla because travelers find their way by it; the Prophet was unique among prophets and through him God guided creation.
THALABI:v10p228/r2.anchor:
قال بعض أهل الكلام في قوله:
ووجدك ضالا فهدى: إن العرب إذا وجدت شجرة في فلاة من الأرض وحيدة

THALABI:v10p228/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r3.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى ومحمد بن علي الترمذي
THALABI:v10p228/r3.claim: They say the Prophet was obscure and unknown, until God guided people to him so that they recognized him and learned of His favor.
THALABI:v10p228/r3.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى ومحمد بن علي الترمذي: ووجدك خاملا لا تذكر ولا تعرف من أنت

THALABI:v10p228/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r4.speaker: بسام بن عبد الله
THALABI:v10p228/r4.claim: He says the Prophet was unaware of his own identity and condition, which God made known to him.
THALABI:v10p228/r4.anchor: قال بسام بن عبد الله: ووجدك ضالا نفسك لا تدري من أنت فعرفك نفسك وحالك

THALABI:v10p228/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق وغيره
THALABI:v10p228/r5.claim: They say the Prophet was lost in love for Abū Ṭālib and God guided him to that love; another view says he was already loving and God led him to his beloved.
THALABI:v10p228/r5.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق وغيره: ووجدك ضالا بحب أبي طالب فهداك إلى حبه

THALABI:v10p228/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p228/r6.claim: The reading of ḍalāl as excessive love is supported by the brothers’ saying that their father was in clear error and by “your old error” about Joseph.
THALABI:v10p228/r6.anchor: دليله قوله سبحانه، إخبارا عن إخوة يوسف إن أبانا لفي ضلال مبين

THALABI:v10p228/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p228/r7.claim: Another view takes ḍalāl as forgetting the promised exception when asked about the Cave Companions, Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; the proof uses ḍalla to mean forget.
THALABI:v10p228/r7.anchor: وقيل: وجدناك ناسيا شأن الاستثناء حين سئلت عن أصحاب الكهف وذي القرنين والروح

THALABI:v10p228/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r8.speaker: سهل
THALABI:v10p228/r8.claim: He says the Prophet’s natural self, driven by desire, was redirected to the path of knowledge and religious law.
THALABI:v10p228/r8.anchor:
وقال سهل: وجد نفسك نفس الشهوة
والطبع، فغيره إلى سبيل المعرفة والشرع

THALABI:v10p228/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r9.speaker: جنيد
THALABI:v10p228/r9.claim: He says the Prophet was perplexed about explaining the revealed Book, and God guided him to explain it to people.
THALABI:v10p228/r9.anchor: قال جنيد: وجدك متحيرا في بيان الكتاب المنزل عليك فهداك لبيانه

THALABI:v10p228/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r10.speaker: بندار بن الحسين
THALABI:v10p228/r10.claim: He says God made Himself known directly and enriched the Prophet with knowledge, without need for witnesses or proofs.
THALABI:v10p228/r10.anchor: قال بندار بن الحسين: ليس قائما مقام الاستدلال فتعرفت إليك، وأغنيتك بالمعرفة عن الشواهد والأدلة

THALABI:v10p228/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p228/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p228/r11.claim: Another view says the Prophet sought the direction of prayer without knowing it, and God guided him to it.
THALABI:v10p228/r11.anchor: وقيل: وجدك طالبا لقبلتك ضالا عنها فهداك إليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109/r1.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, the Prophet had been unaware of prophethood, then God guided him through prophethood to the religion most rightly guided and most beloved to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (في رواية عطاء) (¬4) ووجدك ضالا عن النبوة فهداك بالنبوة إلى أرشد الأديان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Shahr ibn Ḥawshab say the Prophet was unaware of the signs of prophethood and the rulings of the law, then was guided to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r1.anchor: (وشهر بن حوشب) (¬8) (¬9) ووجدك ضالا عن معالم النبوة وأحكام الشريعة غافلا عنها فهداك إليها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r2.claim: This is the position of the theologians and the author's school: the Messenger was never an unbeliever; they cite 12:3 and 42:52.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r2.anchor: وهذا مذهب أرباب الأصول، وعلماء أصحابنا (¬10) على أن رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r3.claim: He likewise interprets the verse as saying the Prophet did not yet know the Qurʾān and religious law, then God guided him to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r3.anchor: واختار أبو إسحاق (أيضا) (¬1) هذا القول فقال: معناه أنه لم يكن يدري القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r4.claim: On the surface reading, the Prophet was an unbeliever among misguided people and God guided him to monotheism.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r4.anchor: وجرى بعض المفسرين على ظاهر الآية، فقال الكلبي: {ووجدك ضالا}. يعني كافرا في قوم ضلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r5.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says the Prophet followed the way of his people for forty years.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: كان على أمر قومه أربعين سنة (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
