WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid says he was astray from guidance and God guided him to His religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ووجدك ضالا. يعني عن الهدى، فهداك لدينه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r7.speaker: أصحابنا
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r7.claim: They say transmitted evidence is needed to decide the matter, although reason permits someone to be an unbeliever, later receive faith and prophethood, or be stripped of prophethood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p109#2/r7.anchor: قال أصحابنا (¬2): وهذا مما يستدرك بالسماع، فأما العقل فجائز في المعقول أن يكون الشخص كافرا

WAHIDI-QT:93:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:93:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:93:7/r1.claim: Before revelation Muhammad lacked the knowledge of prophethood, Quranic teachings, and law, then God guided him; this connects to 42:52.
WAHIDI-QT:93:7/r1.anchor: { ووجدك ضالا } عما أنت عليه اليوم من معالم النبوة وأحكام القرآن والشريعة فهداك إليها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r2.claim: Being astray means not yet knowing the prophetic signs, Qur'anic rulings, or religious law; God guided him to them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r2.anchor: عما أنت عليه اليوم من معالم النبوة وأحكام القرآن والشريعة، فهداك إليها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r3.claim: He links the explanation to the verse saying Muhammad did not know the Book or faith beforehand.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:93:6-11/r3.anchor: كقوله: ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.claim: He prefers istifā, divine selection: finding a rare valuable thing represents choosing the Prophet from among creatures, a rhetorical emphasis repeated across all three verses.
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r6.anchor: burada fikrimizce bunun en muvâfıkı bu fiillerin ıstıfâ mânasına olmasıdır

ELMALILI:93:6-8/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8/r14.claim: The second clause coordinates with the positive implication of the first rhetorical question, though it may also attach directly to the verb under lam's negation.

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r1.claim: Ḍāll can mean lost, unsure of the way, or astray, but the Prophet was never intellectually or religiously misguided or morally corrupt.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r1.anchor: Resûlullah hiçbir zaman akl ü dinde sapık mânasına dâll olmamıştır

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r2.claim: From the beginning God kept him pure of shirk and desire-driven error; he was a monotheist, never bowed to idols, and was known for virtue and trustworthiness.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r2.anchor: Muvahhid yetişmiş, hiçbir puta secde etmemiş, Allah’tan başka ilâh tanımamış

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r3.claim: Before revelation, despite sound reason, the Prophet lacked revealed knowledge and was perplexed about the true law beyond unaided reason.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r3.anchor: hak din ve şeriatının ne olması lâzım geleceğini ve dünyayı sarmış olan buhran içinden

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r4.claim: He recognized the corruption of pagan Arab religion and the deviation of Judaism and Christianity, yet could not determine the way to truth; the verse refers to this pre-prophetic searching.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r4.anchor: Karşısında bulunan Yahudîlik ve Nasrâniyet, iki dinin çığırından çıkmış olduğunu da sezmişti

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r5.claim: God selected and guided him by revelation and scripture, teaching what he did not know and showing the straight path.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r5.anchor: Verdiği vahiy, indirdiği kitap ile bilmediklerini bildirerek doğru yolu göstermedi mi?

ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.claim: The three blessings show that each later state surpassed the earlier one, assuring the Prophet that this pattern will continue.
ELMALILI:93:6-8#2/r11.anchor: Bunların mâkabline rabtıyla mâna şu olmuş oluyor: Görülüyor ki bunların hepsinde sonu evvelinden hayırlı olmuştur

CORPUSCORANICUM:93:7:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:7:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:7:anmerkung/r1.claim: This is likely the earliest Quranic use of hadā; the idea of personal divine guidance for a successful human life is prominent in biblical and especially psalmic texts, with Syriac dbar a parallel technical term.
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:7:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die durch das Verb ausgedrückte Vorstellung einer persönlichen göttlichen Wegeleitung, die allein ein gelingendes menschliches Leben verbürgt, ist biblisch und besonders im Psalter prominent

CORPUSCORANICUM:93:7:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:7:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:7:anmerkung/r2.claim: Sure 93 also has further motifs and structural links to psalmic lament prayers, especially Psalm 13.
CORPUSCORANICUM:93:7:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Da neben 93:7 keiner dieser Belege zu Gruppe I zu rechnen ist, dürfte es sich beim vorliegenden Vers um das früheste koranische Vorkommnis von hadā handeln.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r3.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r3.claim: Some say Muhammad got lost as a child in a Meccan valley and God enabled him to find his way back to his grandfather.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r3.anchor: Resûlullah küçükken Mekke vadilerinden birinde yolunu şaşırıp kaybolmuştu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r4.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r4.claim: Others say he became lost on the road to Syria with Abu Talib but found his uncle with God's help.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r4.anchor: Resûlullah amcası Ebû Tâlib’le birlikte Suriye’ye giderken yolda kaybolmuştu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r5.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r5.claim: The majority reading compares Muhammad's pre- and post-prophetic life: before revelation he saw his society's beliefs and way of life were wrong but did not know how to guide it; the Qur'an showed him both destination and path.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:93:6/r5.anchor: Kur’an’ı göndererek onu bu durumdan kurtarıp yolunu aydınlattı; ona hem varacağı hedefi hem de o hedefe nasıl varacağını öğretti

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p416/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p416/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p416/r5.claim: God guided the Prophet and guided many people through him, as expressed by the verse that he guides to a straight path.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r1.claim: “He found you astray” cannot mean error opposed to guidance, since prophets are protected from that.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r1.anchor: ووجدك ضالا: لا يمكن حمله على الضلال الذي يقابله الهدى، لأن الأنبياء معصومون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Muḥammad became lost in Mecca’s passes as a child, then God returned him to his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو ضلاله وهو في صغره في شعاب مكة، ثم رده الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r3.claim: Other accounts say he was lost from his wet nurse Ḥalīma or on the Syrian journey with Abū Ṭālib; Abū Ḥayyān rejects interpretations improper to attribute to prophets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r3.anchor: وقيل: ضلاله من حليمة مرضعته. وقيل: ضل في طريق الشام حين خرج به أبو طالب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān recalls a dream interpretation: God found the Prophet’s people astray and guided them through him; this requires an omitted possessive, like “ask the town.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p497/r4.anchor: ووجدك، أي وجد رهطك، ضالا، فهداه بك.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r1.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r1.claim: The clause joins the implication of the preceding question: God found him unaware of revealed laws inaccessible to unaided reason and guided him to them through revelation; al-Wāḥidī says most exegetes and al-Zajjāj prefer this, paralleling the statements that he did not know the Book before revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r1.anchor: عطف على ما يقتضيه الإنكار السابق كما أشير إليه أو على المضارع المنفي بل داخل في حكمه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib reports a childhood journey to Syria with his uncle Abū Ṭālib; a dark-night diversion by Satan is stopped by Gabriel, who sends Satan far away and returns the Prophet to the caravan.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r2.anchor: وروي سعيد بن المسيب أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم سافر مع عمه أبي طالب إلى الشام

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet became lost as a child in Mecca's ravines, and Abū Jahl returned him to his grandfather, who was praying at the Kaʿba; a tale has the camel refuse to move behind him, saying that the leader should ride in front.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r3.anchor: وقيل إشارة إلى ما روي عن ابن عباس من أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ضل وهو صغير عن جده في شعاب مكة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r4.claim: Another account says the child was lost a second time; a heavenly caller directed ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib and Waraqa to find him beneath a simr tree in Wādī Tihāma, playing with its twigs.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r4.anchor: وقيل ضل عليه الصلاة والسلام مرة أخرى وطلبوه فلم يجدوه فطاف عبد المطلب بالكعبة سبعا وتضرع إلى الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r5.claim: A further report says Ḥalīma lost him at Mecca's gate while returning him to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib after weaning; Alusi says these literal wandering accounts are weak as explanations of a divine favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r5.anchor: وقيل أضلته مرضعته حليمة عند باب مكة حين فطمته وجاءت به لترده على عبد المطلب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r6.speaker: الجنيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r6.claim: Al-Junayd interprets the verse as the Prophet being uncertain about the meanings of the revealed Book, then guided to explain it, a sense close to the main interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r6.anchor: وقال الجنيد قدس سره أي وجدك متحيرا في بيان الكتاب المنزل عليك فهداك لبيانه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r7.claim: Other Sufi readings say he was unaware of his own worth until shown his lofty rank, or was guided through love and nearness to knowledge of God; Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says God granted him knowledge of a pre-eternal love.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم وجدك غافلا عن قدر نفسك فأطلعك على عظيم محلك وقيل وجدك ضالا عن معنى محض المودة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r8.speaker: الحريري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r8.claim: Al-Ḥarīrī similarly reads the verse as the Prophet's uncertainty over subtle meanings of love, for which God guided him; Alusi classifies these as mystical interpretations.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r8.anchor: وقال الحريري أي وجدك مترددا في غوامض معاني المحبة فهداك لها وهو أيضا كذلك وكل ذلك منزع صوفي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r9.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān dreamed that a possessive noun is omitted: God found the Prophet's people astray and guided them through him; Alusi dismisses this proposal.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p162/r9.anchor: ورأى أبو حيان في منامه أن الكلام على حذف مضاف والمعنى ووجد رهطك ضالا فهدى بك وهو كما ترى في يقظتك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.claim: The Prophet recounts asking about other prophets' gifts; God reminds him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, provision, an opened breast, and removal of his burden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p455/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "سألت ربي مسألة وودت أني لم أكن سألته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r1.claim: He was unaware of the way he would follow, and God guided him to monotheism and prophethood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r1.anchor: يعني ضالا عما أنت عليه {فهدى} أي: فهداك للتوحيد والنبوة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r2.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r2.claim: They say he was unaware of prophetic signs and the rulings of revealed law, and God guided him to them, as in 12:3 and 42:52.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r2.anchor: قال الحسن والضحاك وابن كيسان: "ووجدك ضالا" عن معالم النبوة وأحكام الشريعة غافلا عنها، فهداك إليها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r3.claim: One view says he was lost in Mecca's mountain paths and was guided to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r3.anchor: وقيل: ضالا في شعاب مكة فهداك إلى جدك عبد المطلب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that as a small child the Prophet became lost in Mecca's ravines; Abu Jahl found him away from his sheep and returned him to Abd al-Muttalib.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ضل في شعاب مكة وهو صبي صغير، فرآه أبو جهل منصرفا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r5.claim: He reports that on a dark journey with Abu Talib and Khadija's servant Maysara, Iblis diverted the Prophet's camel; Gabriel drove Iblis away and returned him to the caravan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع عمه أبي طالب في قافلة ميسرة غلام خديجة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r6.claim: Another view says God let him recognize himself and his condition, since he had not known who he was.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p456/r6.anchor: وقيل: وجدك ضالا [ضال] (4) نفسك لا تدري من أنت، فعرفك نفسك وحالك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r2.claim: ضالا means lacking knowledge of rulings; God then taught him by revelation, inspiration, and enabling sound reflection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r2.anchor: عن علم الحكم والأحكام. { فهدى } فعلمك بالوحي والإلهام والتوفيق للنظر

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r3.claim: Alternative reports say the Prophet lost his way while Abū Ṭālib took him to Syria or while Ḥalīma brought him after weaning; God guided him away from uncle or grandfather.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r3.anchor: وقيل وجدك ضالا في الطريق حين خرج بك أبو طالب إلى الشام

BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.claim: A report promises acceptance among those for whom Muhammad may intercede and deeds equal to the number of orphans and petitioners for reciting al-Ḍuḥā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:93:6-11/r8.anchor: من قرأ سورة والضحى جعله الله سبحانه وتعالى فيمن يرضى

BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.claim: These reminders of earlier favors reassure Muhammad that God will not leave him: God sheltered the orphan, guided the bewildered, and enriched the needy.
BINTSHATI:v1p42/r1.anchor: فهو تعالى يبث في نفس الرسول الطمأنينة ويثبت قلبه بلفته إلى ما أسبغ الله عليه في أولاه من نعم

BINTSHATI:v1p44/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r1.claim: Dalal originally means losing one's way or being bewildered; guidance contrasts with it, first in spatial senses and then metaphorically and religiously.
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r1.anchor: أصل الضلال في الاستعمال اللغوي، من فقدان الطريق: أرض مضلة، يضل فيها. والضلة الحيرة.

BINTSHATI:v1p44/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r2.claim: Although the Quran often uses dalal for unbelief and falsehood, it retains the physical sense, shown by its repeated association with the path and by 32:10.
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r2.anchor: مع بقاء الملحظ الحسي اللغوي الذي هو ضلال الطريق، بدليل إقتران الضلال بالسبيل، عشرين مرة

BINTSHATI:v1p44/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r3.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r3.claim: Al-Razi attributes to al-Kalbi, al-Suddi, and Muqatil the view that Muhammad followed his people's religion for forty years.
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r3.anchor: ذكره "الرازي" معزواً إلى الكلبي والسدي ومقاتل

BINTSHATI:v1p44/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r4.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r4.claim: Most commentators reject the unbelief interpretation because prophets are held immune from major and minor sins before and after their commission, let alone unbelief.
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r4.anchor: وأنكره جمهور المفسرين، وردوه بأن الأنبياء يجب أن يكونوا معصومين، قبل النبوة وبعدها

BINTSHATI:v1p44/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r5.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r5.claim: Al-Razi alone lists twenty interpretations of dalal here, including losing the direction of prayer, being unable to emigrate, and losing one's way in worldly trade.
BINTSHATI:v1p44/r5.anchor: وذهبوا بعد ذلك في تأويل الضلال، مذاهب شتى بلغت، في تفسير

BINTSHATI:v1p45/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r1.claim: The timeline rules out reading dalal as trade or a wish to emigrate: Muhammad had left commerce for retreat before revelation, and migration came years after this early surah.
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r1.anchor: كف عن شواغل التجارة قبل المبعث منذ آثر الاعتكاف والخلوة في غار حراء

BINTSHATI:v1p45/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r2.speaker: الزمخشري وأبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan report stories that Muhammad was lost in Mecca as a child, lost from Halima, or lost on the road to Syria.
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r2.anchor: ضل في شعاب مكة وهو صغير، فرده الله إلى جده، وقيل ضلاله من حليمة مرضعته

BINTSHATI:v1p45/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan recounts a dream resolving the verse as Muhammad's people being astray and guided through him, with an omitted noun like people in ask the town.
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r3.anchor: وجدك ضالاً فهدى، أي وجد رهطك ضالاً فهداه بك. على حذف المضاف، أي رهط.

BINTSHATI:v1p45/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r4.claim: Quranic usage itself shows dalal need not mean unbelief; Joseph's brothers use it for their father's intense attachment to Joseph.
BINTSHATI:v1p45/r4.anchor: وليس الضلال هنا كفراً، وإنما هو الشغف بيوسف

BINTSHATI:v1p46/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r1.claim: Other Quranic uses describe passionate love, Moses acting before knowing, or one witness forgetting and needing a reminder; none means unbelief.
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r1.anchor: وليس شيء من هذه الآيات بالذي يحمل الضلال فيه، على معناه الاصطلاحي وهو الكفر

BINTSHATI:v1p46/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r2.claim: Reading the verse through Quranic usage avoids both equating dalal with unbelief and inventing twenty strained interpretations to protect Muhammad from that charge.
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r2.anchor: يعفينا من التزام المصطلح في لفظ الضلال بمعنى الكفر، وهو أيضاً يعفينا من تلك التأويلات العشرين

BINTSHATI:v1p46/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r3.claim: It is implausible to make God's favor consist of returning a lost child to his family or making Muhammad's trade profitable.
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r3.anchor: وغريب عندنا كذلك، أن نتصور أن الله من على رسوله، بأنه رده إلى أهله

BINTSHATI:v1p46/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r4.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines dalal as leaving the straight way, deliberately or by mistake, slightly or greatly.
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r4.anchor: إنه ترك الطريق المستقيمة عمداً كان أو سهواً، قليلاً كان أو كثيراً

BINTSHATI:v1p46/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r5.claim: Before revelation Muhammad was perplexed: he rejected his people's ways but did not know the straight path or how to escape them.
BINTSHATI:v1p46/r5.anchor: فقد كانت حالته قبل المبعث حالة حيرة: عاف حال قومه وأنكرها، ولكن أين الطريق المستقيم؟

BINTSHATI:v1p47/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r1.claim: Muhammad remained perplexed until revelation guided him to the true religion and clear path; this is also Muhammad Abduh's conclusion.
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r1.anchor: ولبث على حيرته أمداً، حتى جاءته الرسالة فهدته إلى الدين القيم وأبانت له سواء السبيل

BINTSHATI:v1p47/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r2.claim: This account makes Abu Hayyan's dream and hypothetical omitted noun unnecessary.
BINTSHATI:v1p47/r2.anchor: ونحن بهذا في غنى عما لجأ إليه أبو حيان في رؤياه، من افتراض مضاف محذوف

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.claim: God's care did not restore Muhammad's dead father or fill his treasury; it preserved his character and prepared him psychologically for the message.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r2.anchor: وليست وقاية مادية ترد إليه أباه الذي مات قبل مولده، وتملأ خزانته بالمال

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.claim: Using the heart-verb wajada foregrounds the Prophet's inner state and emotional reassurance, rather than merely listing external circumstances.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r3.anchor: الفعل {وَجَدَ} وهو من أفعال القلوب ولم يقل مثلاً

BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.claim: The omitted objects after sheltered, guided, and enriched are not merely for rhyme: the open wording can include both Muhammad and those helped through his mission.
BINTSHATI:v1p51/r4.anchor: ونضيف إليها فائدة الإطلاق، فتحتمل: فآواك وآوى برسالتك اليتامى والمستضعفين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r1.claim: Ḍāll means that the Prophet did not know the revealed religious laws, not that he followed idolatry; 42:52 similarly says he did not know the Book or faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r1.anchor: إلا ما عملت بالعقل الصحيح والفطرة السليمة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r2.claim: The text names the consequence, being without guidance in law, for its cause: having no one to teach the Prophet the law.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r2.anchor: فأطلق اللازم وهو الضلال على الملزوم , والمسبب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r3.claim: He retained sound reason and natural monotheistic faith, but God withheld a teacher of religious law so reflection could lead him to truth in fundamentals.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r3.anchor: إلا ما عملت بالعقل الصحيح والفطرة السليمة المستقيمة من التوحيد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r4.claim: God then guided him comprehensively through revelation, inspiration, and the direction to reasoned inquiry.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p457/r4.anchor: فعلمك بالوحي والإلهام والتوفيق للنظر ما لم تكن تعلم

DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.claim: When the Prophet compared himself with earlier prophets' miracles, God reminded him of shelter, guidance, enrichment, an opened breast, removal of burden, and raised renown.
DURR-FULL:v8p543/r7.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته

DURR-FULL:v8p544/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r3.claim: He says God found Muhammad among misguided people and rescued him from their misguidance.
DURR-FULL:v8p544/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ووجدك ضالا فهدى} قال: وجدك بين ضالين فاستنقذك من ضلالتهم

TAB:93:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:6/r2.speaker: author
TAB:93:6/r2.claim: On the neighboring verse, al-Tabari says God found Muhammad unlike the person he had become by the time of revelation.
TAB:93:6/r2.anchor: ووجدك على غير الذي أنت عليه اليوم

TAB:93:6/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:6/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB:93:6/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Muhammad followed the way of his people for forty years.
TAB:93:6/r3.anchor: عن السدي ووجدك ضالا قال :  كان على أمر قومه أربعين عاما

TAB:93:6/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:93:6/r4.speaker: قيل
TAB:93:6/r4.claim: Another view takes the phrase to mean that God found Muhammad among a people astray and guided him.
TAB:93:6/r4.anchor: وقيل :  عني بذلك :  ووجدك في قوم ضلال فهداك

BURHAN:v2p331/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p331/r7.claim: A report question is semantically affirmative, so an explicit affirmative clause can coordinate with it, as in “Did He not find you an orphan, then shelter you, and find you astray, then guide you?”
BURHAN:v2p331/r7.anchor: فالاول كقوله ﴿ ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى ووجدك ضالا فهدى ﴾ 5 وقوله ﴿ ألم نشرح لك صدرك

ITQAN:v3p124/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p124/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p124/r3.claim: A concordant metaphor joins meanings that can coexist: making someone alive represents guiding the lost, and life and guidance could meet in one thing.
ITQAN:v3p124/r3.anchor: أي ضالا فهديناه استعير الإحياء من جعل الشيء حيا للهداية

ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.claim: Laf wa-nashr names two or more items and then corresponding details, either item by item or collectively, leaving listeners to match each detail to what fits.
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r1.anchor: هو أن يذكر شيئان أو أشياء إما تفصيلا بالنص على كل واحد أو إجمالا بأن يؤتى بلفظ يشتمل على متعدد

ITQAN:v3p251#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r7.claim: Mujahid and others understand the person not to be repelled as a seeker of knowledge; the injunction is paired with God finding the Prophet lost and guiding him.
ITQAN:v3p251#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ وأما السائل فلا تنهر ﴾ راجع إلى قوله ﴿ ووجدك ضالا ﴾ فإن المراد السائل عن العلم كما فسره مجاهد وغيره

DAMGHANI:v1p445/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r2.claim: ميت can mean one who is astray, as in the metaphor of being brought from misguidance to guidance.
DAMGHANI:v1p445/r2.anchor: الثانى : الموت الضلاله . قوله تعالى فى سورة الانعام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r1.claim: The entry treats وجد as a past-tense verb.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r1.anchor: وجد : فعل ماض . وهو في الأصل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r2.claim: The root originally means encountering or sensing something after it had not been so perceived.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r2.anchor: وهو في الأصل : إصابة الشيء والإحساس به بعد أن لم يكن ذلك

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r3.claim: The entry gives distinct usage forms for finding lost property, feeling grief or anger, and finding or having means in money.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r3.anchor: يقال وجدت الضالة وحدانا . ووجدت من الحزن وجدا . ومن الغضب موجدة . ووجدت في المال وجدا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r4.claim: Ibn Faris transmits وجدانا as a form used for anger and cites an anonymous verse using وجدان for intense resentment.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r4.anchor: قال ابن فارس : وحكى بعضهم : وجدت في الغضب وجدانا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r9.claim: A fifth face is seeing: the source includes the commands to kill opponents wherever found and the address, 'He found you astray and guided you.'
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p615/r9.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن وجد في القرآن على ستة أوجه : -

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254/r1.claim: Ḍalāl can mean confusion or deviation from the truth or the road, as in the description of the Prophet before guidance.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254/r1.anchor: الضلال: الحيرة والعدول عن الحق والطريق، يقال: ضل عن الحق

NASHR:v2p409/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p409/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASHR:v2p409/r1.claim: In a report, God reminds Muhammad that He found him orphaned, astray, and poor, then sheltered, guided, and enriched him; the exchange also recalls expanded breast and raised fame.
NASHR:v2p409/r1.anchor: ومنهم من يحيي الموتى قال يا محمد: ألم أجدك يتيما فآويتك؟

NASHR:v2p409/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p409/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p409/r2.claim: Takbīr at the end is fitting because the sūra has just recounted divine favors.
NASHR:v2p409/r2.anchor: فكان التكبير عند نهاية ذكر النعم أنسب

ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r1.claim: The Prophet cannot have been astray in the sense opposite to guidance, because prophets are protected from that.
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r1.anchor: لا يمكن حمله على الضلال الذي يقابله الهدى ، لأن الأنبياء معصومون من ذلك

ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet got lost as a child in Mecca's ravines and God returned him to his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muttalib.
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هو ضلاله وهو في صغره في شعاب مكة ، ثم رده الله إلى جده عبد المطلب

ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r3.claim: Another account says he was lost from his wet nurse Halima.

ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r4.claim: A further account says he lost his way on the journey to Syria with Abu Talib.
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r4.anchor: وقيل : ضل في طريق الشام حين خرج به أبو طالب

ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān criticizes some exegetical claims as impermissibly attributing things to prophets.
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r5.anchor: ولبعض المفسرين أقوال فيها بعض ما لا يجوز نسبته إلى الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام

ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r6.claim: In a dream reflection, Abū Ḥayyān considers that God found the Prophet's people astray and guided them through him.
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r6.anchor: ولقد رأيت في النوم أني أفكر في هذه الجملة فأقول على الفور : { ووجدك } ، أي وجد رهطك ، { ضالاً } ، فهداه بك

ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r7.claim: This reading can be parsed with a deleted genitive, as in the expression ask the town, meaning its people.
ABUHAYYAN:93:7/r7.anchor: ثم أقول : على حذف مضاف ، نحو : { وسئل القرية }

ALUSI:93:7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:7/r1.claim: The clause is coordinated either with what the preceding rhetorical question implies or with the verb negated by lam, under the same negation.
ALUSI:93:7/r1.anchor: عطف على ما يقتضيه الإنكار السابق كما أشير إليه أو على المضارع المنفي بلم داخل في حكمه

ALUSI:93:7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:7/r2.claim: The main interpretation is that the Prophet did not know the revealed laws that reason alone cannot discover; revelation then guided him to them and taught him what he had not known.
ALUSI:93:7/r2.anchor: فهدك إلى مناهجها في تضاعيف ما أوحى إليك من الكتاب المبين وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم

ALUSI:93:7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r3.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI:93:7/r3.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says most commentators hold this interpretation, and al-Zajjāj also chooses it.
ALUSI:93:7/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا كما قال الواحدي أكثر المفسرين وهو اختيار الزجاج

ALUSI:93:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
ALUSI:93:7/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib relates that, during a dark night on the journey to Syria with Abū Ṭālib, Satan led the Prophet's camel off course; Gabriel drove Satan away and returned the camel to the caravan.
ALUSI:93:7/r4.anchor: روى سعيد بن المسيب أن صلى الله عليه وسلم سافر مع عمه أبي طالب إلى الشام

ALUSI:93:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:7/r5.claim: Some say the verse alludes to Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib's report about Satan diverting the Prophet on the Syrian journey and Gabriel restoring him to the caravan.
ALUSI:93:7/r5.anchor: فما في الآية إشارة إلى ذلك على ما قيل

ALUSI:93:7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:93:7/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for a story in which the child Muhammad became lost in Mecca's ravines; Abū Jahl found him while returning from his flocks and brought him back to his grandfather, who was praying at the Kaʿba.
ALUSI:93:7/r6.anchor: وقيل إشارة إلى ما روي عن ابن عباس من أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ضل وهو صغير عن جده في شعاب مكة

ALUSI:93:7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:93:7/r7.claim: In the same story, Abū Jahl's camel refused to move with Muhammad behind him but rose when he placed him in front; the camel supposedly asked how the leader could follow the follower.
ALUSI:93:7/r7.anchor: فكانت الناقة تقول يا أحمق هو الإمام فكيف يقوم خلف المقتدي

ALUSI:93:7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:7/r8.claim: Another account says the Prophet was lost a second time; ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib circled the Kaʿba seven times, then a heavenly caller directed him and Waraqa to the child under a samar tree in Tihāma.
ALUSI:93:7/r8.anchor: وقيل ضل عليه الصلاة والسلام مرة أخرى وطلبوه فلم يجدوه فطاف عبد المطلب بالكعبة سبعاً

ALUSI:93:7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:7/r9.claim: A further report says his wet nurse Ḥalīma lost him near Mecca's gate while returning him to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib after weaning.
ALUSI:93:7/r9.anchor: وقيل أضلته مرضعته حليمة عند باب مكة حين فطمته وجاءت به لترده على عبد المطلب

ALUSI:93:7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:7/r10.claim: Reading the verse as a literal childhood loss on a road is weak: such an event would not count among the divine favors being recounted here.
ALUSI:93:7/r10.anchor: وضعف حمل الآية على ذلك بأن مثله بالنسبة إلى ما تقدم لا يعد من نعم الله تعالى

ALUSI:93:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:7/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes ḍāll as a lone tree in the desert and means that God found the Prophet alone, then guided people to him rather than leaving him isolated.
ALUSI:93:7/r11.anchor: وقيل الضال الشجرة المنفردة في البيداء ليس حولها شجر والمراد أما وجدك وحدك ليس معك أحد

ALUSI:93:7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r12.speaker: الجنيد
ALUSI:93:7/r12.claim: Al-Junayd reads the verse as the Prophet being perplexed about explaining the revealed Book, then being guided to its explanation, a reading close to the main interpretation.
ALUSI:93:7/r12.anchor: وقال الجنيد قدس سره أي وجدك متحيراً في بيان الكتاب المنزل عليك فهداك لبيانه

ALUSI:93:7/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r13.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:93:7/r13.claim: Some mystics say God found the Prophet unaware of his own worth and disclosed his great standing.
ALUSI:93:7/r13.anchor: وقال بعضهم وجدك غافلاً عن قدر نفسك فأطلعك على عظيم محلك

ALUSI:93:7/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:7/r14.claim: A mystical reading says he lacked understanding of pure love, so God gave him the cup of nearness and affection and guided him to divine knowledge.
ALUSI:93:7/r14.anchor: وقيل وجدك ضالاً عن معنى محض المودة فسقاك كأساً من شراب القربة والمودة

ALUSI:93:7/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r15.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ALUSI:93:7/r15.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says the Prophet was unaware, in eternity, of God's love for him, and God then bestowed knowledge of Himself; this resembles the preceding mystical view.
ALUSI:93:7/r15.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه كنت ضالاً عن محبتي لك في الأزل فمننت عليك بمعرفتي

ALUSI:93:7/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r16.speaker: الحريري
ALUSI:93:7/r16.claim: Al-Ḥarīrī says the Prophet was uncertain amid the subtleties of love's meanings and was guided to them.
ALUSI:93:7/r16.anchor: وقال الحريري أي وجدك متردداً في غوامض معاني المحبة فهداك لها

ALUSI:93:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r17.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI:93:7/r17.claim: Abū Ḥayyān once dreamed the phrase omitted a possessive noun, meaning God found the Prophet's people astray and guided them through him.
ALUSI:93:7/r17.anchor: ورأى أبو حيان في منامه أن الكلام على حذف مضاف والمعنى ووجد رهطك ضالاً فهدى بك

ALUSI:93:7/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:7/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:7/r18.claim: Al-Ālūsī dismisses Abū Ḥayyān's dream interpretation with a wry remark that it is evident even while awake.

ALUSI:93:8/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r16.speaker: عصام الدين
ALUSI:93:8/r16.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn suggests orphan means lacking a teacher, lost means lacking knowledge, and having dependents means the religious community needing guidance; God enriched the Prophet with revelation. Al-Ālūsī finds this strained.
ALUSI:93:8/r16.anchor: وذكر عصام الدين في هذه الآيات أنه يحتمل أن يراد باليتيم فاقد المعلم

ALUSI:93:8/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the proposed allegory of orphanhood, misguidance, and dependents as deficiencies of teaching and knowledge is plainly strained.

ALUSI:93:8/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:93:8/r18.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because they are clear from context and to preserve the verse endings.
ALUSI:93:8/r18.anchor: وحذف المفعول في الأفعال الثلاثة لظهور المراد مع رعاية الفواصل

ALUSI:93:8/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:93:8/r19.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:93:8/r19.claim: Another explanation says the omitted objects signal expansive generosity: God sheltered, guided, and enriched the Prophet and those connected with him; al-Ālūsī objects that the following fa-clauses resist this.
ALUSI:93:8/r19.anchor: وقيل ليدل على سعة الكرم والمراد آواك وآوى لك وبك وهداك ولك وبك وأغناك ولك وبك وظاهر الفاء مع تلك الأفعال نأبى ذلك

BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet asking about gifts given to other men; God reminds him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him. Other transmitters add that God expanded his breast and removed his burden.
BAGHAWI:93:6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : " قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته

BAGHAWI:93:7/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:7/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:93:7/r1.claim: He was astray from the state he now has, and God guided him to monotheism and prophethood.
BAGHAWI:93:7/r1.anchor: يعني ضالاً عما أنت عليه فهداك للتوحيد والنبوة

BAGHAWI:93:7/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:7/r2.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وابن كيسان
BAGHAWI:93:7/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Kaysan say he was unaware of prophetic signs and the law before revelation, and God guided him to them.

BAGHAWI:93:7/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:7/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:93:7/r3.claim: Another view says he was lost in Mecca's valleys and God guided him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
BAGHAWI:93:7/r3.anchor: وقال : ضالاً في شعاب مكة فهداك إلى جدك عبد المطلب

BAGHAWI:93:7/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:93:7/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that as a small child the Prophet became lost in Mecca's valleys; Abu Jahl found him turning away from his flock and returned him to Abd al-Muttalib.
BAGHAWI:93:7/r4.anchor: روى أبو الضحى عن ابن عباس  "  أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ضل في شعاب مكة وهو صبي صغير

BAGHAWI:93:7/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:7/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
BAGHAWI:93:7/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib recounts that during a night journey with Abu Talib's caravan, the Devil led Muhammad's camel off course; Gabriel blew the Devil to Abyssinia and returned Muhammad to the caravan.
BAGHAWI:93:7/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب : خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع عمه أبي طالب في قافلة مسيرة غلام خديجة فبينما هو راكب

BAGHAWI:93:7/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:93:7/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BAGHAWI:93:7/r6.claim: Another view says God found him not knowing himself or his identity, then made him know himself and his condition.
BAGHAWI:93:7/r6.anchor: وقيل : وجدك ضالاً ضال نفسك لا تدري من أنت ،   فعرفك نفسك وحالك .

BAYDAWI:93:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:93:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:93:7/r1.claim: The Prophet lacked knowledge of rulings; God guided him by revelation, inspiration, and enabling reflection.
BAYDAWI:93:7/r1.anchor: عن علم الحكم والأحكام فهدى فعلمك بالوحي والإلهام والتوفيق للنظر

BAYDAWI:93:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:93:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:93:7/r2.claim: Another account says he was lost on the road when Abū Ṭālib took him to Syria, or when Ḥalīma brought him after weaning to return him to his grandfather; God removed the loss involving his uncle or grandfather.
BAYDAWI:93:7/r2.anchor: وقيل وجدك ضالا في الطريق حين خرج بك أبو طالب إلى الشام أو حين فطمتك حليمة

BIQAI:93:7/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:7/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:7/r1.claim: Here ḍāll means not yet knowing revealed laws, not actual religious deviation: the Prophet had never followed his people's religion; lack of knowledge is called by its consequence, and the verse 42:52 confirms he had not known scripture or faith.
BIQAI:93:7/r1.anchor: لأنه لم يكن على دين قومه في حين من الأحيان أصلاً

BIQAI:93:7/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:7/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:7/r2.claim: The usual chain is orphanhood, a caregiver's neglect, and consequent ignorance; thus the verse names the result, misguidance, for its cause, lack of knowledge.
BIQAI:93:7/r2.anchor: يلزم من اليتم في الغالب عدم العلم لليتيم لتهاون الكافل

BIQAI:93:7/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:7/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:7/r3.claim: Before revelation, sound reason and original nature had already led him to monotheism and related truths; he refrained from actions whose rulings he did not know, and this sound nature is a form of piety.
BIQAI:93:7/r3.anchor: إلا ما علمت بالعقل الصحيح والفطرة السليمة المستقيمة من التوحيد وبعض توابعه

BIQAI:93:7/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:93:7/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:93:7/r4.claim: God then gave him comprehensive guidance, teaching what he had not known through revelation, inspiration, and enabling him to reason correctly.
BIQAI:93:7/r4.anchor: فعلمك بالوحي والإلهام والتوفيق للنظر ما لم تكن تعلم

DURR:93:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:6/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:93:6/r5.claim: The Prophet recalls asking for a favor he wished he had not requested; God reminds him of shelter as an orphan, guidance, wealth, an opened breast, relief of burden, and raised renown, and he affirms each favor.
DURR:93:6/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «سألت ربي مسألة ووددت أني لم أكن سألته ، فقلت : قد كانت قبلي الأنبياء

DURR:93:7/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:93:7/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:93:7/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God found Muhammad among people astray and rescued him from their misguidance.
DURR:93:7/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله : { ووجدك ضالاً فهدى } قال : وجدك بين ضالين فاستنقذك من ضلالتهم .

IBNASHUR:93:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:7/r1.claim: Ḍalāl is failing to find the route to a desired destination, whether by taking another route or remaining unsure which way to go; the latter is intended here.
IBNASHUR:93:7/r1.anchor: وهو المقصود هنا لأن المعنى : أنك كنت في حيرة من حال أهل الشرك

IBNASHUR:93:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:7/r2.claim: The Prophet was perplexed by his people's polytheism, recognized through God's inspiration that it was wrong, and was moved to seek truth so he would be ready to receive revelation.
IBNASHUR:93:7/r2.anchor: فأراكه الله غير محمود وكرهه إليك ولا تدري ماذا تتبع من الحق

IBNASHUR:93:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:7/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:7/r3.claim: The verse does not mean that the Prophet followed falsehood: the author's scholars agree that prophets are protected from associating partners with God before prophethood.
IBNASHUR:93:7/r3.anchor: وليس المراد بالضلال هنا اتباع الباطل

IBNASHUR:93:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:7/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:7/r4.claim: Scholars differ over prophets' immunity from major universally indecent sins before prophethood: rigorous scholars among the author's school exempt them, while the Muʿtazila deny such immunity because reason can identify grave wrongs.
IBNASHUR:93:7/r4.anchor: وإنما اختلفوا في عصمتهم من نوع الذنوب الفواحش التي لا تختلف الشرائع

IBNASHUR:93:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:7/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:7/r5.claim: The author's school agrees that the Prophet did nothing against the fundamentals of religion before his mission; his well-attested uprightness and purity are evidence for his prophethood.
IBNASHUR:93:7/r5.anchor: لم يصدر منه ما ينافي أصول الدين قبل رسالته

IBNASHUR:93:7/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:7/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:7/r6.claim: The Qurʾān challenges people to consider that the Prophet lived among them long before revelation and asks whether they knew their Messenger; polytheists never answered his censure by claiming he shared their wrongdoing.
IBNASHUR:93:7/r6.anchor: ولأنه لم يؤثر أن المشركين أفحموا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما أنكر عليهم

IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.claim: The objects of the three verbs are omitted because the preceding second-person pronouns make them understood; the ellipsis is concise and preserves the verse endings.
IBNASHUR:93:8/r3.anchor: للعلم بها من ضمائر الخطاب قبلها ، وحدفها إيجاز

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r1.speaker: الحسن والضحاك وفرقة
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and a group understand the phrase as God finding him outside the prophetic way and guiding him through prophethood and messengership.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r1.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن والضحاك وفرقة ،   والضلال يختلف ،   فمنه القريب ومنه البعيد

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r2.claim: He distinguishes remote unbelief from the Prophet's nearer state of not yet discerning the path: he followed no one's way but searched and considered.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r2.anchor: وكان هذا الضلال الذي ذكره الله تعالى لنبيه عليه السلام أقرب ضلال وهو الكون واقفا لا يميز المهيع

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says the Prophet remained on his people's practice for forty years.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r3.anchor: وقال السدي : أقام على أمر قومه أربعين سنة

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r4.claim: Another view takes the phrase to mean that people attributed misguidance to him.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r4.anchor: وقيل معنى { وجدك ضالاً } أي تنسب إلى الضلال

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r5.speaker: الكلبي
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī says God found him among a misguided people, so he seemed to be one of them.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي ووجدك في قوم ضلال فكأنك واحد منهم

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r6.claim: The Prophet never worshipped an idol; he did eat their slaughter, observed some customs while recognizing their error, left ʿArafāt, and differed from them in many matters.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد : ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يعبد صنماً قط ،   ولكنه أكل ذبائحهم حسب حديث زيد

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r7.speaker: زيد بن عمرو
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r7.claim: The passage invokes a report of Zayd ibn ʿAmr concerning the Prophet eating sacrificial meat at the lower part of Baldah.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r7.anchor: حسب حديث زيد بن عمرو في أسفل بلدح

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet was lost as a small child in Mecca's ravines, then God returned him to his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس هو ضلاله وهو صغير في شعاب مكة ،   ثم رده الله تعالى إلى جده عبد المطلب

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r9.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r9.claim: Another view says this refers to his being lost from Ḥalīma, his wet nurse.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r9.anchor: وقيل هو ضلاله من حليمة مرضعته

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r10.speaker: الترمذي وعبد العزيز بن يحيى
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r10.claim: Al-Tirmidhī and ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā say ḍāll means obscure and unknown, after which God made people know him.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r10.anchor: وقال الترمذي وعبد العزيز بن يحيى : { ضالاً } معناه خامل الذكر لا يعرفك الناس

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r11.claim: He prefers the meaning of not yet knowing the way, citing 42:52, where the Prophet had not known the Book or faith.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r11.anchor: والصواب أنه ضلال من توقف لا يدري كما قال عز وجل : { ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان }

IBNATIYYA:93:7/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r12.speaker: أهل السنة
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r12.claim: Thaʿlab reports Ahl al-Sunna's view that the phrase refers to his giving his daughter in marriage during the pre-Islamic period, and similar matters.
IBNATIYYA:93:7/r12.anchor: قال ثعلب قال أهل السنة : هو تزويجه بنته في الجاهلية ونحوه

IBNKATHIR:93:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:93:7/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir links the phrase to 42:52: Muhammad did not know the Book or faith until revelation was made a light by which God guides and he guides to a straight path.
IBNKATHIR:93:7/r1.anchor: كقوله { وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا

IBNKATHIR:93:7/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:7/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR:93:7/r2.claim: Some say Muhammad was lost among the ravines of Mecca as a child, then found his way back.

IBNKATHIR:93:7/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:7/r3.speaker: قيل، حكاه البغوي
IBNKATHIR:93:7/r3.claim: Another account says that while traveling to Syria with his uncle, Muhammad's camel was diverted at night by Iblis; Gabriel blew Iblis away toward Abyssinia and guided the mount back to the road.
IBNKATHIR:93:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : إنه ضل وهو مع عمه في طريق الشام ،   وكان راكبا ناقة في الليل

IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.claim: Qatada says these three conditions were the Messenger's circumstances before God sent him as a prophet.
IBNKATHIR:93:8/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله : { أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوَى

KASHSHAF:93:7/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:7/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:7/r1.claim: Ḍāllan means lacking knowledge of revealed religious law and matters learned through transmission, as in the verse “you did not know the Book.”
KASHSHAF:93:7/r1.anchor: معناه الضلال عن علم الشرائع وما طريقه السمع

KASHSHAF:93:7/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:7/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:7/r2.claim: One account says he was lost as a child in a ravine near Mecca and Abū Jahl returned him to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
KASHSHAF:93:7/r2.anchor: وقيل : ضل في صباه في بعض شعاب مكة ، فردّه أبو جهل إلى عبد المطلب

KASHSHAF:93:7/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:7/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:7/r3.claim: Another account says Ḥalīma lost him at Mecca's gate after weaning him and bringing him back to ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
KASHSHAF:93:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : أضلته حليمة عند باب مكة حين فطمته وجاءت به لتردّه على عبد المطلب

KASHSHAF:93:7/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:7/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:7/r4.claim: A third account says he lost his way on the Syria journey with Abū Ṭālib.
KASHSHAF:93:7/r4.anchor: وقيل : ضلّ في طريق الشام حين خرج به أبو طالب

KASHSHAF:93:7/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:7/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:7/r5.claim: God guided him by teaching him the Qurʾān and religious laws, or by removing him from the error of his grandfather and uncle.
KASHSHAF:93:7/r5.anchor: فهداك : فعرفك القرآن والشرائع .   أو فأزال ضلالك عن جدك وعمك

KASHSHAF:93:7/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:93:7/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:93:7/r6.claim: If being with his people for forty years means lacking revealed knowledge, that is acceptable; if it means sharing their religion and unbelief, it is impossible, since prophets are protected from blameworthy sins before and after prophecy.
KASHSHAF:93:7/r6.anchor: فإن أراد أنه كان على خلوّهم عن العلوم السمعية ،   فنعم ؛ وإن أراد أنه كان على دينهم وكفرهم ،   فمعاذ الله

MAWARDI:93:7/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r1.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI:93:7/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĪsā says God found the Prophet not knowing the truth and guided him to it.
MAWARDI:93:7/r1.anchor: أحدها : وجدك لا تعرف الحق فهداك إليه ،   قاله ابن عيسى

MAWARDI:93:7/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r2.speaker: الطبري
MAWARDI:93:7/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes it as God finding him without prophethood and guiding him to it.
MAWARDI:93:7/r2.anchor: الثاني : ووجدك ضالاً عن النبوة فهداك إليها ،   قاله الطبري

MAWARDI:93:7/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:93:7/r3.claim: Al-Suddī's sense is that God found the Prophet's people astray and guided him to show them the way.
MAWARDI:93:7/r3.anchor: الثالث : ووجد قومك في ضلال فهداك إلى إرشادهم ،   وهذا معنى قول السدي

MAWARDI:93:7/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:7/r4.claim: Another possibility is that God found him away from the migration and guided him to it.
MAWARDI:93:7/r4.anchor: ووجدك ضالاً عن الهجرة فهداك إليها

MAWARDI:93:7/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:7/r5.claim: It may mean forgetful, with God reminding him, as in the wording about one of the two women forgetting.
MAWARDI:93:7/r5.anchor: الخامس : ووجدك ناسياً فأذكرك ،   كما قال تعالى : { أن تضل إحداهما }

MAWARDI:93:7/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:7/r6.claim: It may mean seeking: he was seeking the direction of prayer, and the lost person is called seeking because he searches for the way.
MAWARDI:93:7/r6.anchor: السادس : ووجدك طالباً القبلة فهداك إليها ،   ويكون الضلال بمعنى الطلب ،   لأن الضال طالب

MAWARDI:93:7/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:7/r7.claim: It may mean perplexed: he was uncertain how to explain what had been revealed, and a lost person is perplexed.
MAWARDI:93:7/r7.anchor: السابع : ووجدك متحيراً في بيان ما نزل عليك فهداك إليه ،   فيكون الضلال بمعنى التحير

MAWARDI:93:7/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:7/r8.claim: It may mean lost or neglected among his people, with God guiding him to Himself; a lost person is also one who is forsaken.
MAWARDI:93:7/r8.anchor: الثامن : ووجدك ضائعاً في قومك فهداك إليه ،   ويكون الضلال بمعنى الضياع

MAWARDI:93:7/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI:93:7/r9.claim: It may mean loving guidance: God found him loving it and led him to it; the cited verse uses dalāl for Jacob's love, and two poetic lines offer further evidence.
MAWARDI:93:7/r9.anchor: التاسع : ووجدك محباً للهداية فهداك إليها ،   ويكون الضلال بمعنى المحبة

MAWARDI:93:7/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:93:7/r10.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI:93:7/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads it with the lost one as subject and passive guidance: God found the astray one, who was then guided through you.
MAWARDI:93:7/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ووجدَك ضالٌّ فهُدِي ،   أي وجَدَك الضالُّ فاهتدى بك

NASAFI:93:7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:7/r1.claim: “Astray” means not yet knowing the signs of prophethood, the laws of the revealed way, or the path of revelation; God then taught him the laws and Qurʾān.
NASAFI:93:7/r1.anchor: أي غير عالم ولا واقف على معالم النبوة وأحكام الشريعة

NASAFI:93:7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:7/r2.claim: Another account says he lost the road to Syria while traveling with Abū Ṭālib, who returned him to the caravan.
NASAFI:93:7/r2.anchor: وقيل : ضل في طريق الشام حين خرج به أبو طالب فرده إلى القافلة

NASAFI:93:7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:93:7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:93:7/r3.claim: This cannot mean deviation from truth: from the beginning until revelation he was protected from idol worship and the filthy conduct of sinners.
NASAFI:93:7/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يفهم به عدول عن حق ووقوع في غي فقد كان عليه الصلاة السلام من أول حاله إلى نزول الوحي عليه معصوماً من عبادة الأوثان وقاذورات أهل الفسق والعصيان

QURTUBI:93:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:7/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi first explains the phrase as Muhammad being unaware of what prophethood meant for him, then God guiding him; here error means heedlessness, as in verses about God not being heedless and Muhammad once being among the heedless.
QURTUBI:93:7/r1.anchor: أي غافلا عما يراد بك من أمر النبوة ، فهداك : أي أرشدك . والضلال هنا بمعنى الغفلة

QURTUBI:93:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r2.speaker: الضحاك وشهر بن حوشب
QURTUBI:93:7/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and others say he did not know the Qur'an or religious law, and God guided him to them, as in 42:52.
QURTUBI:93:7/r2.anchor: وقال قوم : " ضالا " لم تكن تدري القرآن والشرائع ، فهداك اللّه إلى القرآن ، وشرائع الإسلام ، عن الضحاك وشهر بن حوشب وغيرهما

QURTUBI:93:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r3.speaker: الكلبي والفراء
QURTUBI:93:7/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Farra say he was among a misguided people and God guided them through him.
QURTUBI:93:7/r3.anchor: وقال قوم : " ووجدك ضالا " أي في قوم ضلال ، فهداهم اللّه بك . هذا قول الكلبي والفراء

QURTUBI:93:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r4.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI:93:7/r4.claim: Al-Suddi gives a similar sense: Muhammad's people were astray, and God guided him to show them the way.
QURTUBI:93:7/r4.anchor: وعن السدي نحوه ، أي ووجد قومك في ضلال ، فهداك إلى إرشادهم

QURTUBI:93:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r5.claim: Another view says God found him seeking the migration and guided him to it.
QURTUBI:93:7/r5.anchor: وقيل : " ووجدك ضالا " عن الهجرة ، فهداك إليها

QURTUBI:93:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r6.claim: Another explanation is that God reminded him to make an exception when asked about the People of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, as in the verse about one of two women erring.
QURTUBI:93:7/r6.anchor: وقيل : " ضالا " أي ناسيا شأن الاستثناء حين سئلت عن أصحاب الكهف وذي القرنين والروح – فأذكرك

QURTUBI:93:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r7.claim: Another view says he was seeking the direction of prayer and God guided him to it, citing the turning of his face toward heaven.
QURTUBI:93:7/r7.anchor: وقيل : ووجدك طالبا للقبلة فهداك إليها . بيانه

QURTUBI:93:7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r8.claim: Another explanation makes him perplexed about explaining what had been revealed, then guided to its explanation.
QURTUBI:93:7/r8.anchor: وقيل : ووجدك متحيرا عن بيان ما نزل عليك ، فهداك إليه

QURTUBI:93:7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r9.claim: Another view says he was lost or obscure among his people, and God guided him to them.
QURTUBI:93:7/r9.anchor: وقيل : ووجدك ضائعا في قومك ، فهداك إليه

QURTUBI:93:7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r10.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق وغيره
QURTUBI:93:7/r10.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq and others say he loved Abu Talib and God guided him to love his Lord.
QURTUBI:93:7/r10.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق وغيره : " ووجدك ضالا " : تحب أبا طالب ، فهداك إلى محبة ربك

QURTUBI:93:7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r11.speaker: بسّام بن عبد الله
QURTUBI:93:7/r11.claim: Bassam ibn Abd Allah says he was unaware of himself, and God made him know himself and his state.
QURTUBI:93:7/r11.anchor: وقال بسام بن عبد الله : " ووجدك ضالا " بنفسك لا تدري من أنت ، فعرفك بنفسك وحالك

QURTUBI:93:7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r12.speaker: الجنيدي
QURTUBI:93:7/r12.claim: Al-Junayd says he was perplexed about explaining the Book, so God taught him its exposition, as in verses assigning the Prophet to explain revelation and disputes.
QURTUBI:93:7/r12.anchor: وقال الجنيدي : ووجدك متحيرا في بيان الكتاب ، فعلمك البيان

QURTUBI:93:7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:7/r13.claim: Some theologians say Arabs call a solitary tree in a wasteland a dallah because travelers use it to find the way; al-Qurtubi prefers this as it gathers the figurative readings: Muhammad stood alone in his religion and God guided creation through him.
QURTUBI:93:7/r13.anchor: وقال بعض المتكلمين : إذا وجدت العرب شجرة منفردة في فلاة من الأرض ، لا شجر معها ، سموها ضالة

QURTUBI:93:7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:7/r14.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the solitary-tree interpretation is most appealing because it gathers the figurative interpretations of the verse.
QURTUBI:93:7/r14.anchor: قلت : هذه الأقوال كلها حسان ، ثم منها ما هو معنوي ، ومنها ما هو حسي . والقول الأخير أعجب إلي

QURTUBI:93:7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r15.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI:93:7/r15.claim: Some say he outwardly followed the general customs of his people for forty years without openly opposing them, while shirk should not be attributed to him.
QURTUBI:93:7/r15.anchor: وقال قوم : إنه كان على جملة ما كان القوم عليه ، لا يظهر لهم خلافا على ظاهر الحال ، فأما الشرك فلا يظن به

QURTUBI:93:7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r16.speaker: الكلبي والسدي
QURTUBI:93:7/r16.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Suddi take the phrase literally as saying he was an unbeliever with an unbelieving people; al-Qurtubi points back to its rebuttal in Surat al-Shura.
QURTUBI:93:7/r16.anchor: وقال الكلبي والسدي : هذا على ظاهره ، أي وجدك كافرا والقوم كفار فهداك

QURTUBI:93:7/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:93:7/r17.claim: Al-Qurtubi says he already treated and refuted this attribution in Surat al-Shura.
QURTUBI:93:7/r17.anchor: وقد مضى هذا القول والرد عليه في سورة " الشورى "

QURTUBI:93:7/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r18.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r18.claim: Another view says he was immersed among the people of shirk and God distinguished him from them, like water lost within milk.
QURTUBI:93:7/r18.anchor: وقيل : وجدك مغمورا بأهل الشرك ، فميزك عنهم . يقال : ضل الماء في اللبن

QURTUBI:93:7/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r19.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r19.claim: Another view takes dalal to mean love: God found him loving guidance and led him to it; the word is used for love in the cited verse and poetry.
QURTUBI:93:7/r19.anchor: ويكون الضلال بمعنى المحبة . ومنه قوله تعالى

QURTUBI:93:7/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r20.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:93:7/r20.claim: An anonymous poet uses dalal in the sense of love, supporting this lexical interpretation.
QURTUBI:93:7/r20.anchor: قال الشاعر : هذا الضلال أشاب مني المفرقا *** والعارضين ولم أكن متحققا

QURTUBI:93:7/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r21.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI:93:7/r21.claim: Al-Hasan's explanatory reading has the straying one become guided through the Prophet: God found the lost one and he was guided by you.
QURTUBI:93:7/r21.anchor: وفي قراءة الحسن " ووجدك ضال فهدى " أي وجدك الضال فاهتدى بك

QURTUBI:93:7/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r22.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r22.claim: A final view says his people did not know his worth, so God guided Muslims to him until they believed in him.
QURTUBI:93:7/r22.anchor: وقيل : " ووجدك ضالا " لا يهتدي إليك قومك ، ولا يعرفون قدرك ، فهدى المسلمين إليك

QURTUBI:93:7/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r23.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:93:7/r23.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts that Muhammad was lost in Mecca's ravines as a child; Abu Jahl found him away from his sheep and returned him to his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib.
QURTUBI:93:7/r23.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ضل النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم وهو صغير في شعاب مكة ، فرآه أبو جهل منصرفا عن أغنامه ، فرده إلى جده عبدالمطلب

QURTUBI:93:7/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r24.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI:93:7/r24.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr recounts that Satan diverted the Prophet's camel from the road during a dark journey with Abu Talib, until Gabriel cast Satan away to India and returned the Prophet to the caravan.
QURTUBI:93:7/r24.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير : خرج النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم مع عمه أبي طالب في سفر ، فأخذ إبليس بزمام الناقة في ليلة ظلماء

QURTUBI:93:7/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r25.speaker: كعب
QURTUBI:93:7/r25.claim: Ka'b tells how Halima's infant Muhammad disappeared as she returned him to Mecca; signs at the idols and a heavenly voice led Abd al-Muttalib to find him beneath a tree.
QURTUBI:93:7/r25.anchor: وقال كعب : إن حليمة لما قضت حق الرضاع ، جاءت برسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم لترده على عبد المطلب

QURTUBI:93:7/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:93:7/r26.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:93:7/r26.claim: Another view places this guidance on the night of the Ascension, when Gabriel left him and God guided him to the base of the Throne.
QURTUBI:93:7/r26.anchor: وقيل : " ووجدك ضالا " ليلة المعراج ، حين انصرف عنك جبريل وأنت لا تعرف الطريق ، فهداك إلى ساق العرش

RAZI:93:6/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r11.claim: A debt of beneficence is harder to discharge than a financial debt: pardon does not cancel it, it lasts a lifetime, and great gifts are impossible to repay fully.

RAZI:93:6/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:6/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:93:6/r12.claim: The response is to shelter orphans, guide people and provide for them as God did; even good works depend on God’s enabling and guidance.
RAZI:93:6/r12.anchor: الطريق إلى ذلك أن تفعل في حق عبيدي ما فعلته في حقك

RAZI:93:7/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r1.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI:93:7/r1.claim: Some say the Prophet was initially an unbeliever, then God guided him and made him a prophet.
RAZI:93:7/r1.anchor: أن بعض الناس ذهب إلى أنه كان كافرا في أول الأمر

RAZI:93:7/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r2.speaker: القائلون بذلك
RAZI:93:7/r2.claim: Those alleging prior unbelief cite verses about not knowing Scripture or faith, being among the unaware, and the consequence of associating partners.
RAZI:93:7/r2.anchor: على ذلك بآيات أخر منها قوله

RAZI:93:7/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r3.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI:93:7/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says he was an unbeliever among a misguided people, then guided to monotheism.
RAZI:93:7/r3.anchor: الكلبي : { وجدك ضالا } يعني كافرا في قوم

RAZI:93:7/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r4.speaker: السدي
RAZI:93:7/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says the Prophet followed his people’s religion for forty years.
RAZI:93:7/r4.anchor: السدي : كان على دين قومه أربعين سنة

RAZI:93:7/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r5.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI:93:7/r5.claim: Mujāhid says he was astray from his religion’s guidance.
RAZI:93:7/r5.anchor: مجاهد : { وجدك ضالا } عن الهدى لدينه

RAZI:93:7/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r6.speaker: الجمهور من العلماء
RAZI:93:7/r6.claim: The majority agree that the Prophet never disbelieved in God, even for a moment; Rāzī endorses this conclusion.
RAZI:93:7/r6.anchor: وأما الجمهور من العلماء فقد اتفقوا على أنه عليه السلام ما كفر بالله لحظة واحدة

RAZI:93:7/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI:93:7/r7.claim: The Muʿtazila consider prior unbelief rationally impossible because it would repel people from the Prophet.
RAZI:93:7/r7.anchor: المعتزلة : هذا غير جائز عقلا لما فيه من التنفير

RAZI:93:7/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r8.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI:93:7/r8.claim: Rāzī’s school says it is rationally possible for an unbeliever to receive faith and prophethood, though it did not occur here.
RAZI:93:7/r8.anchor: وعند أصحابنا هذا غير ممتنع عقلا لأنه جائز في العقول أن يكون الشخص كافرا

RAZI:93:7/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r9.claim: Scriptural proof excludes that possibility in the Prophet’s case: his companion neither strayed nor erred.
RAZI:93:7/r9.anchor: هذا الجائز لم يقع وهو قوله تعالى : { ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى }

RAZI:93:7/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب
RAZI:93:7/r10.claim: They interpret this as being unaware of divine favor and revealed law, then guided to them; they connect it with verses about not knowing Scripture and being among the unaware.
RAZI:93:7/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب

RAZI:93:7/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r11.claim: One story says the infant became lost from wet nurse Ḥalīma; at Hubal the idols fell and a voice foretold their destruction by the child.
RAZI:93:7/r11.anchor: ضل عن مرضعته حليمة حين أرادت أن ترده إلى جده

RAZI:93:7/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:7/r12.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says he was lost as a small child from his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, nearly died of hunger, and was guided back; a camel moved only when he sat in front.
RAZI:93:7/r12.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : «ضللت عن جدي عبد المطلب وأنا صبي ضائع

RAZI:93:7/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:93:7/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God returned him to his grandfather through an enemy’s hand, as Moses was preserved through his enemy.
RAZI:93:7/r13.anchor: ابن عباس : رده الله إلى جده بيد عدوه

RAZI:93:7/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r14.claim: Another account says a disbeliever took the camel’s reins while the Prophet traveled with Khadīja’s servant Maysara; Gabriel appeared as a man and guided him to the caravan.
RAZI:93:7/r14.anchor: لما خرج مع غلام خديجة ميسرة أخذ كافر بزمام بعيره حتى ضل

RAZI:93:7/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r15.claim: A separate report says Abū Ṭālib took him toward Syria, lost the road, and God guided him.
RAZI:93:7/r15.anchor: وقيل : إن أبا طالب خرج به إلى الشام فضل عن الطريق فهداه الله تعالى

RAZI:93:7/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r16.claim: Water is called ḍalla when submerged at night; the verse can mean the Prophet was hidden among Meccan unbelievers until God strengthened him to make His religion known.
RAZI:93:7/r16.anchor: يقال : ضل الماء في الليل إذا صار مغمورا

RAZI:93:7/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r17.claim: Arabs call a solitary tree in open country a lost one; the Prophet was a unique tree bearing faith’s fruit in a barren land, and God guided people through him.
RAZI:93:7/r17.anchor: العرب تسمي الشجرة الفريدة في الفلاة ضالة

RAZI:93:7/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:7/r18.claim: The saying that wisdom is the believer’s lost property parallels the unique-tree interpretation.

RAZI:93:7/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r19.claim: As a child he lacked knowledge of God; God created in him reason, guidance and knowledge, so ḍāll means lacking knowledge, not holding false belief.
RAZI:93:7/r19.anchor: وجدك ضالا عن معرفة الله تعالى حين كنت طفلا صبيا

RAZI:93:7/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r20.claim: He was unaware of the prophethood he would receive and had no expectation of it; God guided him to a mission Jews and Christians expected only among Israelites.
RAZI:93:7/r20.anchor: كنت ضالا عن النبوة ما كنت تطمع في ذلك ولا خطر شيء من ذلك في قلبك

RAZI:93:7/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r21.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r21.claim: A master may be addressed while the intended referent is his people: they were astray, and God guided them through the Prophet and his law.
RAZI:93:7/r21.anchor: قد يخاطب السيد ،   ويكون المراد قومه

RAZI:93:7/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r22.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r22.claim: It may mean he was separate from the astray and distant from their religion; God then guided him to mix with them and call them to the manifest faith.
RAZI:93:7/r22.anchor: وجدك ضالا عن الضالين منفردا عنهم مجانبا لدينهم

RAZI:93:7/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r23.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r23.claim: It may refer to his uncertainty and wish to leave Quraysh before God authorized emigration; God then guided him to Umm Maʿbad’s tent and the episode of Surāqa.
RAZI:93:7/r23.anchor: وجدك ضالا عن الهجرة ،   متحيرا في يد قريش

RAZI:93:7/r24.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r24.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r24.claim: Another explanation is uncertainty whether the Kaʿba would become his qibla; God guided him toward the qibla he desired.
RAZI:93:7/r24.anchor: كان يتمنى أن تجعل الكعبة قبلة له وما كان يعرف أن ذلك

RAZI:93:7/r25.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r25.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r25.claim: When Gabriel first appeared, the Prophet did not know who he was and was terrified; God guided him until he recognized Gabriel.
RAZI:93:7/r25.anchor: حين ظهرها له جبريل عليه السلام في أول أمره ما كان يعرف أهو جبريل أم لا

RAZI:93:7/r26.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r26.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r26.claim: Ḍalāl can mean love, as in Jacob’s love for Joseph; the Prophet was a lover whom God guided to laws by which he could serve his Beloved.
RAZI:93:7/r26.anchor: الضلال بمعنى المحبة كما في قوله

RAZI:93:7/r27.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r27.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r27.claim: It may mean he lacked worldly and commercial knowledge; God guided him to profitable trade, and Khadīja consequently desired him.
RAZI:93:7/r27.anchor: ضالا عن أمور الدنيا لا تعرف التجارة ونحوها

RAZI:93:7/r28.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r28.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r28.claim: He was powerless and mistreated among his people, who would not accept him as a subordinate; God strengthened him until he became their commander.
RAZI:93:7/r28.anchor: فقوي أمرك وهداك إلى أن صرت آمرا واليا عليهم

RAZI:93:7/r29.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r29.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r29.claim: He did not know the paths of the heavens until God guided him by taking him up on the night journey.
RAZI:93:7/r29.anchor: كنت ضالا ما كنت تهتدي على طريق السموات فهديتك

RAZI:93:7/r30.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r30.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r30.claim: Ḍalāl may mean forgetfulness; awe on the night journey made him forget the praise due, and God taught him to say he could not enumerate His praise.
RAZI:93:7/r30.anchor: نسي ما يجب أن يقال بسبب الهيبة

RAZI:93:7/r31.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r31.speaker: author
RAZI:93:7/r31.claim: Although he knew God inwardly, he did not openly display opposition to his people, and this outward stance was called ḍalāl.
RAZI:93:7/r31.anchor: وإن كان عارفا بالله بقلبه إلا أنه كان في الظاهر لا يظهر لهم خلافا

RAZI:93:7/r32.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:7/r32.speaker: علي عليه السلام
RAZI:93:7/r32.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet’s account that God blocked two youthful intentions to join Meccan entertainments by making him sleep until sunrise; after those occasions he intended no evil until receiving the message.
RAZI:93:7/r32.anchor: روى علي عليه السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : «ما هممت بشيء

RAZI:93:8/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r22.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI:93:8/r22.claim: A report has the Prophet ask for privileges given to Abraham, Moses, David and Solomon; God recalls these favors, opening his breast, raising his mention, removing his burden, giving him al-Baqara’s closing verses, and offering friendship as with Abraham.
RAZI:93:8/r22.anchor: سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أسألها

RAZI:93:8/r23.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:93:8/r23.speaker: القاضي
RAZI:93:8/r23.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that prophets would not ask this without permission, so the report cannot plausibly portray the Prophet asking and God responding with a reprimand.
